units.slavonic_incipit: Во ст҃ы́й и҆ вели́кїй Пѧто́къ ст҃ы̑ѧ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: во стый и великий пяток стыя и спсительныя
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Во ст҃ы́й и҆ вели́кїй Пѧто́къ ст҃ы̑ѧ и҆ сп҃си́тєльныѧ и҆ стра́шныѧ Стрⷭ҇ти соверша́емъ, Гдⷭ҇а и҆ Бг҃а Сп҃са на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хрⷭ҇та̀, ꙗ҆́же на́съ ра́ди во́лею прїѧ́тъ, ѡ҆плева́нїа, бїе́нїа, заꙋше́нїа, доса́ды, насмѣѧ́нїа, багрѧни́цꙋ ѻ҆де́ждꙋ, тро́сть, гꙋ́бꙋ, ѻ҆́цетъ, гво́здїа, копїѐ, и҆ по си́хъ всѣ́хъ, крⷭ҇тъ и҆ сме́рть: ꙗ҆̀же всѧ̑ въ Пѧто́къ содѣ́ѧшасѧ. По внегда́ бо на три́десѧтихъ сре́бреницѣхъ, ѿ дрꙋ́га и҆ ᲂу҆ченика̀ про́данъ бы́въ предаде́сѧ, пре́жде ко А҆́ннѣ вво́дитсѧ а҆рхїере́ю, и҆́же посыла́етъ є҆го̀ къ Каїа́фѣ: и҆дѣ́же ѡ҆плева́нъ бы́сть, и҆ заꙋша́емь по лани́тѣ, кꙋ́пнѡ же порꙋга́емь и҆ посмѣха́емь, слы́шаше: прорцы̀ на́мъ Хрⷭ҇тѐ, кто́ є҆сть ᲂу҆да́ривый тѧ̀; Та́мѡ же и҆ лжесвидѣ́тели прїидо́ша ѡ҆клевета́ющїи, ꙗ҆́кѡ речѐ: разори́те хра́мъ се́й, и҆ тремѝ де́ньми воздви́гнꙋ и҆̀: и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ речѐ Себѐ Сн҃а Бж҃їа, є҆гда̀ и҆ а҆рхїере́й хꙋлы̀ не терпѧ̀, ри́зꙋ свою̀ растерза̀. Оу҆́трꙋ же бы́вшꙋ, ѿво́дитсѧ къ Пїла́тꙋ въ претѡ́ръ: и҆ ті́и не внидо́ша, гле́тъ, да не ѡ҆сквернѧ́тсѧ, но да ꙗ҆дѧ́тъ па́схꙋ. Па́схꙋ же ве́сь пра́здникъ гле́тъ, и҆лѝ и҆ тогда̀ бы́сть, ꙗ҆́коже подоба́ше: Хрⷭ҇то́съ же пре́жде є҆дина́гѡ днѐ сїю̀ сотворѝ зако́ннꙋю Па́схꙋ, сзакла́тисѧ хотѧ̀ въ Пѧто́къ. И҆зше́дъ же Пїла́тъ, вопроша́етъ ѧ҆̀: ѡ҆ чесо́мъ є҆гѡ̀ ѡ҆глаго́лютъ; и҆ поне́же ничто́же подо́бно ѡ҆брѣ́те ко ѡ҆глаго́ланїю, посыла́етъ є҆гѡ̀ къ Каїа́фѣ. Ѻ҆ни́ же па́ки къ Пїла́тꙋ, ꙗ҆́ко то́й бѣ̀ на є҆гѡ̀ ᲂу҆бі́йство ᲂу҆стремля́ѧйсѧ. Ѻ҆́нъ же гле́тъ: поими́те є҆го̀ вы̀ и҆ распни́те, и҆ по зако́нꙋ ва́шемꙋ сꙋди́те. Ѻ҆ни́ же па́ки глѧ́тъ: не досто́итъ на́мъ ᲂу҆би́ти никого́же, распѧ́ти Пїла́та поѡщрѧ́юще. Вопроша́етъ же Хрⷭ҇та̀ Пїла́тъ: а҆́ще Цр҃ь І҆ꙋде́ѡвъ є҆́сть: Ѻ҆́нъ же не и҆сповѣ́дꙋетъ, но вѣ́чный, не во̀ ѿ мі́ра сегѡ̀ моѐ Црⷭ҇тво, гле́тъ. Хотѧ́ же ѿпꙋсти́ти є҆го̀ Пїла́тъ, пе́рвѣе ᲂу҆́бѡ ѻ҆нѣ̑мъ гле́тъ, ни є҆ди́ныѧ на него̀ вины̀ бл҃голи́чныѧ ѡ҆брѣта́ти. Та́же є҆ди́наго на кі́йждо пра́здникъ ска́зꙋѧ ѻ҆бы́чай ѿрꙋща́ти предлага́етъ: и҆̀мже ᲂу҆го́денъ Вара́вва па́че Хрⷭ҇та̀ мни́тсѧ. Пїла́тъ же І҆ꙋде́ѡмъ да́рꙋѧ, би́въ І҆и҃са пре́жде, и҆зводи́тъ съ во́ины, во ѡ҆дѣѧ́нїе ѡ҆блоче́на червле́ное, терно́выми же вѣнце́мъ ѡ҆бложе́нна, и҆ въ десни́цꙋ є҆гѡ̀ тро́сть вложи́въ, рꙋга́ема же ѿ во́инѡвъ, ра́дꙋйсѧ, гл҃ющихъ, Цр҃ю̀ І҆ꙋде́йскїй. Ѻ҆ба́че си́це ко бл҃года́ти порꙋга́всѧ, па́ки глаго́летъ Пїла́тъ: ни є҆ди́нꙋ же сме́рти винꙋ̀ ѡ҆брѣта́ю въ не́мъ. Ѻ҆ни́ же, но мы̀ є҆го̀ ᲂу҆мꙋ́чимъ, гл҃юще, ꙗ҆́кѡ себѐ и҆менꙋ́етъ Сн҃а Бж҃їа. Си̑мъ же гл҃ємымъ, І҆и҃съ молча́ше, наро́дъ же крича́ше къ Пїла́тꙋ: распнѝ, распнѝ є҆го̀. Безче́стною бо сме́ртїю ѡ҆бложи́ти є҆го̀ хотѧ́хꙋ, да и҆ средѝ благꙋ́ю є҆гѡ̀ па́мѧть сотворя́тъ. Пїла́тъ же а҆́ки бы срамлѧ́ѧ и҆́хъ, гле́тъ: Цр҃ѧ́ ли ва́шего распнꙋ̀; Ѻ҆ни́ же не и҆мѣ́ти глѧ́тъ и҆́нагѡ цр҃ѧ̀, но ке́сара. Поне́же бо хꙋлꙋ̀ ре́кше, ничто́же ᲂу҆спѣ́ша, да ке́сара возно́сѧтъ, да понѐ си́це неи́стовство и҆спо́лнѧтъ. Глѧ́тъ бо: всѧ́къ, и҆́же царѧ̀ себѐ творѧ́й, себѐ творѧ́й, прерѣка́етъ ке́сарю. Въ си́хъ же сꙋ́щымъ, жена̀ къ Пїла́тꙋ посла̀, сны̀ стра́шными ᲂу҆боя́вшисѧ, ничто́же глаго́лющи, тебѣ̀ и҆ Пра́ведникꙋ ѻ҆́номꙋ: ᲂу҆жѐ бо є҆гѡ̀ ра́ди мнѡ́гаѧ въ нощѝ пострада́хъ, и҆ то́й ᲂу҆боѧ́всѧ, кро́ве ѻ҆́нагѡ винꙋ̀ ѿража́етъ. Ѻ҆ни́ же крича́хꙋ: кро́вь є҆гѡ̀ на на́съ, и҆ на ча́да на̑ша: а҆́ще сегѡ̀ ѡ҆ста́виши свобо́дна, нѣ́си дрꙋ́гъ ке́сарю. Сегѡ̀ ᲂу҆́бѡ ᲂу҆боѧ́всѧ Пїла́тъ, а҆́ще и҆ ѻ҆па́снѡ того̀ вѣ́дый непови́нна, крⷭ҇тномꙋ ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїю и҆здае́тъ, ѿпꙋсти́въ Вара́ввꙋ. Сїѐ же ви́дѣвъ І҆ꙋ́да, сре́бреники пове́ргъ, и҆схо́дитъ, и҆ ше́дъ ᲂу҆давленїю себѐ предадѐ, на древѣ̀ ѡ҆бѣ́сисѧ, послѣди́ же ѕѣ́лѡ надꙋ́всѧ растерза́етсѧ. Во́ини ᲂу҆́бѡ тро́стїю по главѣ̀ [І҆и҃са] порꙋга́юще, ѡ҆бременя́ютъ є҆мꙋ̀ крⷭ҇тъ, та́же ѿ Кѷрині́и Си́мѡна понꙋ́дивше, крⷭ҇тъ понестѝ задѣва́ютъ. Ѿ часꙋ́ же тре́тїегѡ на ло́бнымъ мѣ́стѣ бы́вше, та́мѡ распина́ютъ є҆го̀, ѿ ѻ҆бою́дꙋ томꙋ̀ и҆ дрꙋга̑ѧ два̀ разбо́йника ѡ҆бѣ́сивше, да и҆ Ѻ҆́нъ ꙗ҆́кѡ ѕлодѣ́й вмѣни́тсѧ. Хꙋ́дости же ра́ди, раздѣле́нїе во́ини ри́замъ є҆гѡ̀ полага́ютъ, жре́бїемъ же нешве́нꙋю є҆гѡ̀ ѻ҆де́ждꙋ даю́тъ, всѧ́кое доса́ды премно́жество дѣ́лающе. Не сїа̑ же то́чїю, но и҆ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ сꙋ́щꙋ рꙋга́ющесѧ глаго́лахꙋ: ᲂу҆а̀, разорѧ́ѧй хра́мъ, и҆ тремѝ де́ньми созида́ѧй, спасѝ са́мъ себѐ. И҆ па́ки: и҆ны̑ѧ спасѐ, себѐ ли не мо́жетъ спастѝ; И҆ па́ки: а҆́ще Цр҃ь І҆и҃левъ є҆́сть, да сни́детъ ны́нѣ со крⷭ҇та̀, и҆ вѣ́рꙋемъ въ него̀. И҆ ᲂу҆́бѡ а҆́ще и҆́стинъ гла́съ, подоба́ше несумнѣ́ннѡ къ немꙋ̀ пристꙋпи́ти: не то́чїю бо І҆и҃левъ Цр҃ь познава́шесѧ, но и҆ всегѡ̀ мі́ра. Что́ бо хотѧ́ше, є҆́же помрачи́тисѧ со́лнцꙋ на часы̀ трѝ, и҆ посредѣ̀ ᲂу҆́бѡ днѐ; да всѣ́мъ бꙋ́детъ Стрⷭ҇ть ꙗ҆вле́на. Е҆́же землѝ трѧсти́сѧ, ка́менїю разсѣда́тисѧ, противокꙋра́зное І҆ꙋде́ѡвъ ѡ҆блича́ющымъ, мнѡ́гими тѣлесє́мъ воскреснꙋ́ти, ко ᲂу҆вѣре́нїе ѻ҆́бщагѡ воскрⷭ҇нїа, и҆ ко ꙗ҆вле́нїе Стра́ждꙋщагѡ си́лы. Завѣ́сѣ цр҃ко́вной раздра́тисѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ хра́мꙋ ꙗ҆рѧ́щꙋсѧ, за и҆́же въ не́мъ Стра́ждꙋщемꙋ сла́внаѧ, и҆ мнѡ́гими ѿкрыва́ющꙋ незри̑маѧ. Въ тре́тїй ᲂу҆́бѡ ча́съ распѧ́тсѧ Хрⷭ҇то́съ, ꙗ҆́коже бж҃е́ственный Ма́рко гле́тъ: Ѿ шеста́гѡ же часа̀ до девѧ́тагѡ тма̀ бы́сть, є҆гда̀ и҆ Ло́ггїнъ со́тникъ пресла̑внаѧ ви́дѣвъ, и҆ па́че со́лнца, вельмѝ воззва̀: вои́стиннꙋ Сн҃ъ бѣ̀ Бж҃їй се́й. Ѿ разбо́йникѡвъ ᲂу҆́бѡ є҆ди́нъ досажда́ше І҆и҃сꙋ, дрꙋгі́й же возбраня́ше є҆мꙋ̀, претѧ̀ запрети́тельнѣйше, и҆ Хрⷭ҇та̀ Сн҃а Бж҃їа и҆сповѣ́дꙋетъ: кѣ́рѣ же є҆гѡ̀ Сп҃съ воздаѐ, є҆́же съ собо́ю въ ра́й ѡ҆бѣщава́етъ пребыва́нїе. Всѧ́кой ᲂу҆́бѡ доса́дѣ на не́мъ и҆спо́лншейсѧ, Пїла́тъ и҆ ті́тлъ надписа̀ на не́мъ глаго́лющъ: І҆и҃съ Назарѧни́нъ, Цр҃ь І҆ꙋде́йскїй. А҆́ще и҆ ѻ҆нѝ возбраня́хꙋ не писа́ти си́це: но ꙗ҆́кѡ Ѻ҆́нъ речѐ си́це: Пїла́тъ же, є҆́же писа́хъ, писа́хъ, па́ки проти́въ речѐ. Та́же Сп҃съ возре́кшꙋ: жа́ждꙋ: ѻ҆́цтомъ со ѻ҆цто́мъ є҆мꙋ̀ раствѡрѧ́ютъ. И҆ ре́къ: соверши́шасѧ, прекло́нь гла́вꙋ, предадѐ дꙋ́хъ. Всѣ́мъ же ѿше́дшымъ, Мт҃и є҆гѡ̀ предстоѧ́ше ᲂу҆̀ крⷭ҇та̀, и҆ сестра̀ є҆ѧ̀ Марїа Клеѡ́пова, ю҆́же І҆а́кѡвъ родѝ, Клеѡ́пѣ безча́днꙋ ᲂу҆ме́ршꙋ, є҆щѐ же и҆ І҆ѡа́ннъ люби́мый є҆мꙋ̀ ᲂу҆чн҃къ. Неразꙋ́мнїи ᲂу҆́бѡ І҆ꙋде́е, нижѐ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ тѣлесѐ зрѣ́ти хотѧ́ще, проси́ша Пїла́та, поне́же вели́кїй бѣ̀ де́нь Па́схи, и҆ Пѧто́къ, да ѡ҆сꙋжде́нныхъ го́лени сокрꙋша́тсѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ да скорѣ́е сме́рть прїи́детъ. И҆ ѻ҆́нѣхъ ᲂу҆́бѡ го́лени сокрꙋши́ша, є҆ще́ бо жи́ви бѧ́хꙋ, на І҆и҃са же прише́дше, ꙗ҆́кѡ ви́дѣша є҆гѡ̀ ᲂу҆жѐ ᲂу҆ме́рша, є҆́же сокрꙋши́ти ᲂу҆́бѡ, ѡ҆ста́виша. Є҆ди́нъ же нѣ́кто во́инникъ, Ло́ггїнъ зово́мый, везꙋ́мнымъ ᲂу҆гожда́ѧ, воздви́гъ копїѐ, въ десна̑ѧ рє́бра пробода́етъ Хрⷭ҇та̀: и҆ а҆́бїе и҆зы́де кро́вь и҆ вода̀: є҆́же ᲂу҆́бѡ ꙗ҆́кѡ чл҃вѣ́ка, є҆́же же ꙗ҆́кѡ па́че чл҃вѣ́ка. И҆лѝ, кро́вь ᲂу҆́бѡ бж҃е́ственныхъ ра́ди варе́нїй прича́стїа, вода́ же кр҃ще́нїа ра́ди. То́й бо дво́еточный и҆сто́чникъ вои́стиннꙋ, є҆́же по на́мъ содержи́тъ та́инство: сїа̑ І҆ѡа́ннъ ви́дѣвъ свидѣ́телствова, и҆ и҆́стинно є҆сть свидѣ́телство є҆гѡ̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ предстоѧ̀ при всѣ́хъ и҆ ви́да, пи́шетъ: и҆ а҆́ки а҆́ще бы лꙋ́жнаѧ и҆мѣ́лъ глаго́лати, не бы на безче́стїе ᲂу҆чт҃лю неимѣ́ємаѧ спле́лъ. Се́мꙋ, глѧ́ти, тогда̀ сꙋ́щꙋ, сосꙋ́домъ нѣ́кимъ ѿ живото́чныхъ ре́бръ бж҃е́ственнꙋю и҆ прест҃ꙋ́ю кро́вь прїѧ́ти. Си̑мъ же та́кѡ преесте́ственнѡ содѣ́ѧннымъ, поне́же къ ве́черꙋ бя́ше ᲂу҆жѐ, І҆ѡ́сифъ и҆́же ѿ А҆рїмаѳе́а и҆схо́дитъ, ᲂу҆чн҃къ пре́жде, ꙗ҆́коже про́чїи, ᲂу҆тае́нный, и҆ къ Пїла́тꙋ прише́дъ со дерзнове́нїемъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ зна́емъ сꙋ́щꙋ про́ситъ тѣ́ло І҆и҃сово: Ѻ҆́нъ же вза́ти повелѣва́етъ. И҆ ᲂу҆́бѡ съ крⷭ҇та̀ сїѐ сне́мъ, всебл҃гоговѣ́йнѡ положѝ. И҆ ᲂу҆жѐ прише́дшей но́щи, прихо́дитъ Никоди́мъ, носѧ̀ смѵ́рны и҆ а҆лѡ́й, нѣ́кое смѣше́нїе, состро́еное кре́менемъ, и҆ плащани́цею ѡ҆бви́вше, ꙗ҆́коже ѻ҆бы́чай бѣ̀ І҆ꙋде́ѡмъ твори́ти, близꙋ̀ положи́ша, во и҆зсѣ́ченомъ ѿ ка́мене гро́бѣ І҆ѡ́сифовѣ, и҆дѣ́же никто́же пре́жде лежа̀, да не Хрⷭ҇тꙋ воскр҃шꙋ, и҆но́мꙋ воскрⷭ҇нїе напи́шꙋти. Смѣше́нїю же а҆лѡ́а и҆ смѵ́рны, припѣча́тительнымъ сꙋ́щымъ, є҆ѵа́ггелъ воспомѧнꙋ̀, да є҆гда̀ ви́дѧтъ плащани́цꙋ и҆ сꙋда́рь, во гро́бѣ ѡ҆ста́влены, не непщꙋ́ютъ ᲂу҆кра́денꙋ є҆мꙋ̀ бы́ти: ка́кѡ бо свободѣ̀ толи́цѣй не сꙋ́щей, ꙗ҆́коже и҆ ѿто́ргнꙋти ѻ҆нал си́це взаждє́ннаѧ пло́ти; Сїа̑ всѧ̑ пресла́внѡ бы́вшаѧ къ тогда́шнее Пѧтка̀ вре́мѧ, и҆ на́мъ си́хъ всѣ́хъ па́мѧть твори́ти, со сокрꙋше́нїемъ се́рдца и҆ ᲂу҆миле́нїемъ, бг҃оно́снїи Ѻ҆ц҃ы̀ повелѣ́ша. Вѣ́домо же ᲂу҆́бѡ, ꙗ҆́кѡ въ шесты́й де́нь седми́цы, ꙗ҆́кѣ въ Пѧто́къ распѧ́тсѧ Гдⷭ҇ь, зане́же и҆ къ шесты́й де́нь и҆знача́ла созда́тисѧ человѣ́кꙋ. Но и҆ къ шесты́й ча́съ днѐ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ повѣ́шенъ бы́сть: занѐ къ то́й ча́съ, ꙗ҆́коже глѧ́тъ, и҆ А҆да́мъ на ѡ҆рече́нное дре́во рꙋ́цѣ просте́ръ косни́сѧ, и҆ ᲂу҆́мре: подоба́ше бо въ ѻ҆́ньже ча́съ сокрꙋше́нъ, въ то́й па́ки созда́тисѧ. Въ вертогра́дѣ же, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ А҆да́мъ въ раѝ. Го́рькое питїѐ вкꙋше́нїе ѡ҆бразова́ше. Заꙋше́нїе на́шꙋ свобо́дꙋ ꙗ҆влѧ́ше. Ѻ҆плева́нїе, и҆ безче́стное ѡ҆бхожде́нїе, є҆́же ѡ҆ на́съ че́сти. Терно́вый вѣне́цъ, кла́твы ꙗ҆́же на на́съ ѡ҆гна́нїе. Багрѧ́наѧ ѻ҆де́жда, за кѡ́жаныѧ ри̑зы, и҆ за є҆́же на на́съ црⷭ҇кꙋю ᲂу҆́тварь. Гво́здїе, всеконе́чное на́шегѡ грѣха̀ недвиже́нїе. Крⷭ҇тъ, дре́во є҆́же въ раѝ. Пронзе́наѧ ре́бра А҆да́мово ѡ҆бразова́хꙋ ребро̀, ѿ негѡ́же Є҆́ѵа, ѿ неѧ́же престꙋпле́нїе. Копїѐ, пла́менное ѻ҆рꙋ́жїе мнѣ̀ ѡ҆бхожда́етъ. И҆зъ ре́бръ вода̀, ѻ҆́бразъ кр҃ще́нїа. Кро́вь и҆ тро́сть: и҆́миже на́мъ червле́ными пи́смены, ꙗ҆́кѡ Цр҃ь, дре́внее ѻ҆те́чество дарова̀ и҆ подписа̀. Глаго́летсѧ ᲂу҆́бѡ А҆да́мовѣ главѣ̀ та́мѡ лежа́ти, и҆дѣ́же и҆ Хрⷭ҇то́съ, Глава̀ всѣ́хъ распѧ́тсѧ, кр҃ти́сѧ ᲂу҆́бѡ Хрⷭ҇то́вою Кро́вїю и҆сте́кшею. Ло́бное же мѣ́сто гле́тсѧ, зане́же въ пото́пѣ косте́вшей внѣ̀ землѝ А҆да́мовѣ главѣ̀, ко́сти то́чїю
units.english_cohort_translation: On Holy and Great Friday we celebrate the holy, saving, and dread Sufferings of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ, which He willingly accepted for our sake: the spittings, the beatings, the blows upon the cheek, the insults, the mockings, the purple garment, the reed, the sponge, the vinegar, the nails, the spear, and after all these, the Cross and death—all of which were accomplished on Friday. For after He was betrayed, having been sold by a friend and disciple for thirty pieces of silver, He was first led unto Annas the high priest, who sent Him unto Caiaphas; where He was spat upon, buffeted on the cheek, and mocked and derided, hearing them say: "Prophesy unto us, O Christ, who is he that struck Thee?" There also false witnesses came forward slandering Him, saying that He said: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up"; and that He called Himself the Son of God, whereupon the high priest, unable to bear the blasphemy, tore his clothes. When morning came, He was led unto Pilate in the praetorium; and they went not in, it says, lest they should be defiled, but that they might eat the Passover. For it calls the whole feast the Passover, or it was even then held, as was fitting; but Christ had kept the legal Passover one day before, intending to be sacrificed on Friday. And Pilate going out asked them what accusation they brought against Him; and finding nothing worthy of accusation, he sent Him unto Caiaphas. But they returned again unto Pilate, for they were bent on His murder. And he said: "Take ye Him, and crucify Him, and judge Him according to your law." But they said again: "It is not lawful for us to put any man to death," inciting Pilate to crucify Him. And Pilate asked Christ whether He were the King of the Jews; but He confessed not, but said: "My Kingdom is eternal, not of this world." And Pilate, wishing to release Him, first said unto them that he found in Him no plausible guilt. Then he proposed to release one according to the custom of each feast; but they preferred Barabbas rather than Christ. And Pilate, seeking to gratify the Jews, having first scourged Jesus, brought Him forth with the soldiers, clothed in a scarlet garment, crowned with a crown of thorns, and having a reed placed in His right hand, while the soldiers mocked Him, saying: "Hail, King of the Jews!" Having thus mocked Him to gratify them, Pilate said again: "I find no crime of death in Him." But they said: "Nay, but let us put Him to death, for He calls Himself the Son of God." While these things were spoken, Jesus held His peace; but the people cried unto Pilate: "Crucify, crucify Him!" For they wished to encompass Him with an ignominious death, so that they might blot out even His good memory. But Pilate, as though shaming them, said: "Shall I crucify your King?" And they said that they had no king but Caesar. For having alleged blasphemy and succeeded nothing, they magnified Caesar, that so at least they might fulfill their fury. For they said: "Whosoever makes himself a king makes himself a king, speaks against Caesar." While these things were happening, his wife sent unto Pilate, being terrified by frightening dreams, saying: "Have thou nothing to do with that just Man; for I have suffered many things this night because of Him." And he, being afraid, sought to wash away the guilt of that blood. But they cried out: "His blood be on us and on our children! If thou let this Man go, thou art not Caesar's friend." Pilate, therefore, fearing this, although he well knew Him to be innocent, delivered Him over to the sentence of crucifixion, releasing Barabbas. When Judas saw this, he cast down the pieces of silver and went out, and going away gave himself up to hanging, hanging himself upon a tree; and afterwards, swelling exceedingly, he burst asunder. The soldiers, having mocked Him, beating Him upon the head with a reed, laid the Cross upon Him; then compelling Simon of Cyrene, they laid the Cross upon him to carry it. Being come at the third hour to the Place of the Skull, there they crucified Him, hanging also two other thieves on either side of Him, that He might be numbered as an evildoer. In their greed, the soldiers divided His garments, casting lots for His seamless tunic, committing every excess of insult. Nor was it these things alone, but they mocked Him even while He hung upon the Cross, saying: "Aha, Thou that destroyest the temple and buildest it in three days, save Thyself!" And again: "He saved others, can He not save Himself?" And again: "If He be the King of Israel, let Him now come down from the Cross, and we will believe in Him." And truly, if that cry were sincere, they ought without hesitation to have approached Him; for not only was He acknowledged King of Israel, but of the whole world. For what meant the darkening of the sun for three hours, and that in the middle of the day? That His Passion might be made manifest unto all. And the shaking of the earth, and the rending of the rocks, convicting the hard-heartedness of the Jews; and the bodies of many arising, for the assurance of the general resurrection and for the manifestation of the power of the Sufferer. And the rending of the veil of the temple, as though the temple were indignant at the glorious things suffered by Him Who dwells therein, and revealing the unseen things unto many. At the third hour, then, Christ was crucified, as the divine Mark says; and from the sixth hour until the ninth hour there was darkness, when Longinus the centurion, having seen the most marvelous things, and above all the sun, cried aloud with a great voice: "Truly this was the Son of God!" Of the thieves, indeed, one reviled Jesus, but the other rebuked him with severe reproof, and confessed Christ as the Son of God; and the Savior rewarded his faith, promising him that he should be with Him in paradise. When every insult was fulfilled against Him, Pilate also wrote a title upon Him, saying: "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews." And though they forbade him to write thus, Pilate replied again: "What I have written, I have written." Then the Savior, having said: "I thirst," they mingled for Him vinegar with gall [sic: vinegar with vinegar]. And having said: "It is finished," He bowed His head and gave up the spirit. When all had departed, His Mother stood by the Cross, and her sister Mary the wife of Cleopas, whom James begat when Cleopas died childless, and also John His beloved disciple. The senseless Jews, not wishing the bodies to remain upon the cross, because it was the great day of the Passover and Friday, besought Pilate that the legs of the condemned might be broken, that death might come more swiftly. And they broke the legs of the others, for they were yet alive; but coming unto Jesus, when they saw that He was dead already, they refrained from breaking them. But one of the soldiers, named Longinus, seeking to please the senseless ones, raised his lance and pierced Christ in His right side; and immediately there came out blood and water: the one as of a man, the other as beyond man; or rather, the blood for the sake of the communion of the divine offerings, and the water for the sake of baptism. For that twofold fountain truly contains the mystery concerning us; and John having seen these things bore witness, and his witness is true, for standing by through all things and seeing them, he writes them: and if he were to speak falsehood, he would not have invented things not existing unto the dishonor of the Master. At that time, it is said, he stood by and received the divine and most holy blood from the life-giving side in a certain vessel. When these things had been accomplished in this supernatural manner, because it was already evening, Joseph who was of Arimathea came forward, a disciple beforehand, hidden even as the others, and coming unto Pilate with boldness, as he was known unto him, asked for the body of Jesus; and he commanded it to be given. And taking it down from the Cross, he laid it with all reverence. And when night had already come, Nicodemus came, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, compounded with cedar, and wrapping it in a shroud, as was the manner of the Jews to bury, they laid it nearby, in a tomb hewn out of stone belonging to Joseph, wherein no man had ever yet been laid, lest when Christ arose, the resurrection should be ascribed to another. And the Gospel mentioned the mixture of aloes and myrrh being adhesive, that when they should see the shroud and the napkin left behind in the tomb, they might not suppose Him to have been stolen away; for how could there have been such leisure as to tear off what was thus glued to the flesh? All these most glorious things having occurred at that Friday time, the God-bearing Fathers commanded us also to make memory of all these things with contrition of heart and compunction. It is to be known, then, that on the sixth day of the week, that is on Friday, the Lord was crucified, because on the sixth day also man was created in the beginning. And in the sixth hour of the day He was hung upon the Cross: for in that hour, as they say, Adam also stretched forth his hands and touched the forbidden tree, and died; for it was fitting that in the same hour wherein he was crushed, he should be created anew. And in a garden, even as Adam was in paradise. The bitter drink prefigured the tasting. The buffeting made manifest our freedom. The spitting and dishonorable treatment, the honor that is for our sake. The crown of thorns, the driving away of the curse that was upon us. The scarlet robe, instead of the coats of skins and for the royal adornment upon us. The nails, the utter immobility of our sin. The Cross, the tree in paradise. The pierced side prefigured Adam's rib, from which Eve came, from whom came the transgression. The lance wards off from me the flaming sword. The water from the side, the image of baptism. The blood and the reed: wherewith, as a King, He granted and signed unto us our ancient homeland in scarlet letters. For it is said that Adam's skull lay there, where Christ the Head of all was crucified, and it was baptized by the Blood of Christ which flowed forth. And it is called the Place of the Skull, because when the skull of Adam was washed out upon the earth in the deluge, the bone alone...
units.slavonic_text: Во ст҃ы́й и҆ вели́кїй Пѧто́къ ст҃ы̑ѧ и҆ сп҃си́тєльныѧ и҆ стра́шныѧ Стрⷭ҇ти соверша́емъ, Гдⷭ҇а и҆ Бг҃а Сп҃са на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хрⷭ҇та̀, ꙗ҆́же на́съ ра́ди во́лею прїѧ́тъ, ѡ҆плева́нїа, бїе́нїа, заꙋше́нїа, доса́ды, насмѣѧ́нїа, багрѧни́цꙋ ѻ҆де́ждꙋ, тро́сть, гꙋ́бꙋ, ѻ҆́цетъ, гво́здїа, копїѐ, и҆ по си́хъ всѣ́хъ, крⷭ҇тъ и҆ сме́рть: ꙗ҆̀же всѧ̑ въ Пѧто́къ содѣ́ѧшасѧ. По внегда́ бо на три́десѧтихъ сре́бреницѣхъ, ѿ дрꙋ́га и҆ ᲂу҆ченика̀ про́данъ бы́въ предаде́сѧ, пре́жде ко А҆́ннѣ вво́дитсѧ а҆рхїере́ю, и҆́же посыла́етъ є҆го̀ къ Каїа́фѣ: и҆дѣ́же ѡ҆плева́нъ бы́сть, и҆ заꙋша́емь по лани́тѣ, кꙋ́пнѡ же порꙋга́емь и҆ посмѣха́емь, слы́шаше: прорцы̀ на́мъ Хрⷭ҇тѐ, кто́ є҆сть ᲂу҆да́ривый тѧ̀; Та́мѡ же и҆ лжесвидѣ́тели прїидо́ша ѡ҆клевета́ющїи, ꙗ҆́кѡ речѐ: разори́те хра́мъ се́й, и҆ тремѝ де́ньми воздви́гнꙋ и҆̀: и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ речѐ Себѐ Сн҃а Бж҃їа, є҆гда̀ и҆ а҆рхїере́й хꙋлы̀ не терпѧ̀, ри́зꙋ свою̀ растерза̀. Оу҆́трꙋ же бы́вшꙋ, ѿво́дитсѧ къ Пїла́тꙋ въ претѡ́ръ: и҆ ті́и не внидо́ша, гле́тъ, да не ѡ҆сквернѧ́тсѧ, но да ꙗ҆дѧ́тъ па́схꙋ. Па́схꙋ же ве́сь пра́здникъ гле́тъ, и҆лѝ и҆ тогда̀ бы́сть, ꙗ҆́коже подоба́ше: Хрⷭ҇то́съ же пре́жде є҆дина́гѡ днѐ сїю̀ сотворѝ зако́ннꙋю Па́схꙋ, сзакла́тисѧ хотѧ̀ въ Пѧто́къ. И҆зше́дъ же Пїла́тъ, вопроша́етъ ѧ҆̀: ѡ҆ чесо́мъ є҆гѡ̀ ѡ҆глаго́лютъ; и҆ поне́же ничто́же подо́бно ѡ҆брѣ́те ко ѡ҆глаго́ланїю, посыла́етъ є҆гѡ̀ къ Каїа́фѣ. Ѻ҆ни́ же па́ки къ Пїла́тꙋ, ꙗ҆́ко то́й бѣ̀ на є҆гѡ̀ ᲂу҆бі́йство ᲂу҆стремля́ѧйсѧ. Ѻ҆́нъ же гле́тъ: поими́те є҆го̀ вы̀ и҆ распни́те, и҆ по зако́нꙋ ва́шемꙋ сꙋди́те. Ѻ҆ни́ же па́ки глѧ́тъ: не досто́итъ на́мъ ᲂу҆би́ти никого́же, распѧ́ти Пїла́та поѡщрѧ́юще. Вопроша́етъ же Хрⷭ҇та̀ Пїла́тъ: а҆́ще Цр҃ь І҆ꙋде́ѡвъ є҆́сть: Ѻ҆́нъ же не и҆сповѣ́дꙋетъ, но вѣ́чный, не во̀ ѿ мі́ра сегѡ̀ моѐ Црⷭ҇тво, гле́тъ. Хотѧ́ же ѿпꙋсти́ти є҆го̀ Пїла́тъ, пе́рвѣе ᲂу҆́бѡ ѻ҆нѣ̑мъ гле́тъ, ни є҆ди́ныѧ на него̀ вины̀ бл҃голи́чныѧ ѡ҆брѣта́ти. Та́же є҆ди́наго на кі́йждо пра́здникъ ска́зꙋѧ ѻ҆бы́чай ѿрꙋща́ти предлага́етъ: и҆̀мже ᲂу҆го́денъ Вара́вва па́че Хрⷭ҇та̀ мни́тсѧ. Пїла́тъ же І҆ꙋде́ѡмъ да́рꙋѧ, би́въ І҆и҃са пре́жде, и҆зводи́тъ съ во́ины, во ѡ҆дѣѧ́нїе ѡ҆блоче́на червле́ное, терно́выми же вѣнце́мъ ѡ҆бложе́нна, и҆ въ десни́цꙋ є҆гѡ̀ тро́сть вложи́въ, рꙋга́ема же ѿ во́инѡвъ, ра́дꙋйсѧ, гл҃ющихъ, Цр҃ю̀ І҆ꙋде́йскїй. Ѻ҆ба́че си́це ко бл҃года́ти порꙋга́всѧ, па́ки глаго́летъ Пїла́тъ: ни є҆ди́нꙋ же сме́рти винꙋ̀ ѡ҆брѣта́ю въ не́мъ. Ѻ҆ни́ же, но мы̀ є҆го̀ ᲂу҆мꙋ́чимъ, гл҃юще, ꙗ҆́кѡ себѐ и҆менꙋ́етъ Сн҃а Бж҃їа. Си̑мъ же гл҃ємымъ, І҆и҃съ молча́ше, наро́дъ же крича́ше къ Пїла́тꙋ: распнѝ, распнѝ є҆го̀. Безче́стною бо сме́ртїю ѡ҆бложи́ти є҆го̀ хотѧ́хꙋ, да и҆ средѝ благꙋ́ю є҆гѡ̀ па́мѧть сотворя́тъ. Пїла́тъ же а҆́ки бы срамлѧ́ѧ и҆́хъ, гле́тъ: Цр҃ѧ́ ли ва́шего распнꙋ̀; Ѻ҆ни́ же не и҆мѣ́ти глѧ́тъ и҆́нагѡ цр҃ѧ̀, но ке́сара. Поне́же бо хꙋлꙋ̀ ре́кше, ничто́же ᲂу҆спѣ́ша, да ке́сара возно́сѧтъ, да понѐ си́це неи́стовство и҆спо́лнѧтъ. Глѧ́тъ бо: всѧ́къ, и҆́же царѧ̀ себѐ творѧ́й, себѐ творѧ́й, прерѣка́етъ ке́сарю. Въ си́хъ же сꙋ́щымъ, жена̀ къ Пїла́тꙋ посла̀, сны̀ стра́шными ᲂу҆боя́вшисѧ, ничто́же глаго́лющи, тебѣ̀ и҆ Пра́ведникꙋ ѻ҆́номꙋ: ᲂу҆жѐ бо є҆гѡ̀ ра́ди мнѡ́гаѧ въ нощѝ пострада́хъ, и҆ то́й ᲂу҆боѧ́всѧ, кро́ве ѻ҆́нагѡ винꙋ̀ ѿража́етъ. Ѻ҆ни́ же крича́хꙋ: кро́вь є҆гѡ̀ на на́съ, и҆ на ча́да на̑ша: а҆́ще сегѡ̀ ѡ҆ста́виши свобо́дна, нѣ́си дрꙋ́гъ ке́сарю. Сегѡ̀ ᲂу҆́бѡ ᲂу҆боѧ́всѧ Пїла́тъ, а҆́ще и҆ ѻ҆па́снѡ того̀ вѣ́дый непови́нна, крⷭ҇тномꙋ ѡ҆сꙋжде́нїю и҆здае́тъ, ѿпꙋсти́въ Вара́ввꙋ. Сїѐ же ви́дѣвъ І҆ꙋ́да, сре́бреники пове́ргъ, и҆схо́дитъ, и҆ ше́дъ ᲂу҆давленїю себѐ предадѐ, на древѣ̀ ѡ҆бѣ́сисѧ, послѣди́ же ѕѣ́лѡ надꙋ́всѧ растерза́етсѧ. Во́ини ᲂу҆́бѡ тро́стїю по главѣ̀ [І҆и҃са] порꙋга́юще, ѡ҆бременя́ютъ є҆мꙋ̀ крⷭ҇тъ, та́же ѿ Кѷрині́и Си́мѡна понꙋ́дивше, крⷭ҇тъ понестѝ задѣва́ютъ. Ѿ часꙋ́ же тре́тїегѡ на ло́бнымъ мѣ́стѣ бы́вше, та́мѡ распина́ютъ є҆го̀, ѿ ѻ҆бою́дꙋ томꙋ̀ и҆ дрꙋга̑ѧ два̀ разбо́йника ѡ҆бѣ́сивше, да и҆ Ѻ҆́нъ ꙗ҆́кѡ ѕлодѣ́й вмѣни́тсѧ. Хꙋ́дости же ра́ди, раздѣле́нїе во́ини ри́замъ є҆гѡ̀ полага́ютъ, жре́бїемъ же нешве́нꙋю є҆гѡ̀ ѻ҆де́ждꙋ даю́тъ, всѧ́кое доса́ды премно́жество дѣ́лающе. Не сїа̑ же то́чїю, но и҆ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ сꙋ́щꙋ рꙋга́ющесѧ глаго́лахꙋ: ᲂу҆а̀, разорѧ́ѧй хра́мъ, и҆ тремѝ де́ньми созида́ѧй, спасѝ са́мъ себѐ. И҆ па́ки: и҆ны̑ѧ спасѐ, себѐ ли не мо́жетъ спастѝ; И҆ па́ки: а҆́ще Цр҃ь І҆и҃левъ є҆́сть, да сни́детъ ны́нѣ со крⷭ҇та̀, и҆ вѣ́рꙋемъ въ него̀. И҆ ᲂу҆́бѡ а҆́ще и҆́стинъ гла́съ, подоба́ше несумнѣ́ннѡ къ немꙋ̀ пристꙋпи́ти: не то́чїю бо І҆и҃левъ Цр҃ь познава́шесѧ, но и҆ всегѡ̀ мі́ра. Что́ бо хотѧ́ше, є҆́же помрачи́тисѧ со́лнцꙋ на часы̀ трѝ, и҆ посредѣ̀ ᲂу҆́бѡ днѐ; да всѣ́мъ бꙋ́детъ Стрⷭ҇ть ꙗ҆вле́на. Е҆́же землѝ трѧсти́сѧ, ка́менїю разсѣда́тисѧ, противокꙋра́зное І҆ꙋде́ѡвъ ѡ҆блича́ющымъ, мнѡ́гими тѣлесє́мъ воскреснꙋ́ти, ко ᲂу҆вѣре́нїе ѻ҆́бщагѡ воскрⷭ҇нїа, и҆ ко ꙗ҆вле́нїе Стра́ждꙋщагѡ си́лы. Завѣ́сѣ цр҃ко́вной раздра́тисѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ хра́мꙋ ꙗ҆рѧ́щꙋсѧ, за и҆́же въ не́мъ Стра́ждꙋщемꙋ сла́внаѧ, и҆ мнѡ́гими ѿкрыва́ющꙋ незри̑маѧ. Въ тре́тїй ᲂу҆́бѡ ча́съ распѧ́тсѧ Хрⷭ҇то́съ, ꙗ҆́коже бж҃е́ственный Ма́рко гле́тъ: Ѿ шеста́гѡ же часа̀ до девѧ́тагѡ тма̀ бы́сть, є҆гда̀ и҆ Ло́ггїнъ со́тникъ пресла̑внаѧ ви́дѣвъ, и҆ па́че со́лнца, вельмѝ воззва̀: вои́стиннꙋ Сн҃ъ бѣ̀ Бж҃їй се́й. Ѿ разбо́йникѡвъ ᲂу҆́бѡ є҆ди́нъ досажда́ше І҆и҃сꙋ, дрꙋгі́й же возбраня́ше є҆мꙋ̀, претѧ̀ запрети́тельнѣйше, и҆ Хрⷭ҇та̀ Сн҃а Бж҃їа и҆сповѣ́дꙋетъ: кѣ́рѣ же є҆гѡ̀ Сп҃съ воздаѐ, є҆́же съ собо́ю въ ра́й ѡ҆бѣщава́етъ пребыва́нїе. Всѧ́кой ᲂу҆́бѡ доса́дѣ на не́мъ и҆спо́лншейсѧ, Пїла́тъ и҆ ті́тлъ надписа̀ на не́мъ глаго́лющъ: І҆и҃съ Назарѧни́нъ, Цр҃ь І҆ꙋде́йскїй. А҆́ще и҆ ѻ҆нѝ возбраня́хꙋ не писа́ти си́це: но ꙗ҆́кѡ Ѻ҆́нъ речѐ си́це: Пїла́тъ же, є҆́же писа́хъ, писа́хъ, па́ки проти́въ речѐ. Та́же Сп҃съ возре́кшꙋ: жа́ждꙋ: ѻ҆́цтомъ со ѻ҆цто́мъ є҆мꙋ̀ раствѡрѧ́ютъ. И҆ ре́къ: соверши́шасѧ, прекло́нь гла́вꙋ, предадѐ дꙋ́хъ. Всѣ́мъ же ѿше́дшымъ, Мт҃и є҆гѡ̀ предстоѧ́ше ᲂу҆̀ крⷭ҇та̀, и҆ сестра̀ є҆ѧ̀ Марїа Клеѡ́пова, ю҆́же І҆а́кѡвъ родѝ, Клеѡ́пѣ безча́днꙋ ᲂу҆ме́ршꙋ, є҆щѐ же и҆ І҆ѡа́ннъ люби́мый є҆мꙋ̀ ᲂу҆чн҃къ. Неразꙋ́мнїи ᲂу҆́бѡ І҆ꙋде́е, нижѐ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ тѣлесѐ зрѣ́ти хотѧ́ще, проси́ша Пїла́та, поне́же вели́кїй бѣ̀ де́нь Па́схи, и҆ Пѧто́къ, да ѡ҆сꙋжде́нныхъ го́лени сокрꙋша́тсѧ, ꙗ҆́кѡ да скорѣ́е сме́рть прїи́детъ. И҆ ѻ҆́нѣхъ ᲂу҆́бѡ го́лени сокрꙋши́ша, є҆ще́ бо жи́ви бѧ́хꙋ, на І҆и҃са же прише́дше, ꙗ҆́кѡ ви́дѣша є҆гѡ̀ ᲂу҆жѐ ᲂу҆ме́рша, є҆́же сокрꙋши́ти ᲂу҆́бѡ, ѡ҆ста́виша. Є҆ди́нъ же нѣ́кто во́инникъ, Ло́ггїнъ зово́мый, везꙋ́мнымъ ᲂу҆гожда́ѧ, воздви́гъ копїѐ, въ десна̑ѧ рє́бра пробода́етъ Хрⷭ҇та̀: и҆ а҆́бїе и҆зы́де кро́вь и҆ вода̀: є҆́же ᲂу҆́бѡ ꙗ҆́кѡ чл҃вѣ́ка, є҆́же же ꙗ҆́кѡ па́че чл҃вѣ́ка. И҆лѝ, кро́вь ᲂу҆́бѡ бж҃е́ственныхъ ра́ди варе́нїй прича́стїа, вода́ же кр҃ще́нїа ра́ди. То́й бо дво́еточный и҆сто́чникъ вои́стиннꙋ, є҆́же по на́мъ содержи́тъ та́инство: сїа̑ І҆ѡа́ннъ ви́дѣвъ свидѣ́телствова, и҆ и҆́стинно є҆сть свидѣ́телство є҆гѡ̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ предстоѧ̀ при всѣ́хъ и҆ ви́да, пи́шетъ: и҆ а҆́ки а҆́ще бы лꙋ́жнаѧ и҆мѣ́лъ глаго́лати, не бы на безче́стїе ᲂу҆чт҃лю неимѣ́ємаѧ спле́лъ. Се́мꙋ, глѧ́ти, тогда̀ сꙋ́щꙋ, сосꙋ́домъ нѣ́кимъ ѿ живото́чныхъ ре́бръ бж҃е́ственнꙋю и҆ прест҃ꙋ́ю кро́вь прїѧ́ти. Си̑мъ же та́кѡ преесте́ственнѡ содѣ́ѧннымъ, поне́же къ ве́черꙋ бя́ше ᲂу҆жѐ, І҆ѡ́сифъ и҆́же ѿ А҆рїмаѳе́а и҆схо́дитъ, ᲂу҆чн҃къ пре́жде, ꙗ҆́коже про́чїи, ᲂу҆тае́нный, и҆ къ Пїла́тꙋ прише́дъ со дерзнове́нїемъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ зна́емъ сꙋ́щꙋ про́ситъ тѣ́ло І҆и҃сово: Ѻ҆́нъ же вза́ти повелѣва́етъ. И҆ ᲂу҆́бѡ съ крⷭ҇та̀ сїѐ сне́мъ, всебл҃гоговѣ́йнѡ положѝ. И҆ ᲂу҆жѐ прише́дшей но́щи, прихо́дитъ Никоди́мъ, носѧ̀ смѵ́рны и҆ а҆лѡ́й, нѣ́кое смѣше́нїе, состро́еное кре́менемъ, и҆ плащани́цею ѡ҆бви́вше, ꙗ҆́коже ѻ҆бы́чай бѣ̀ І҆ꙋде́ѡмъ твори́ти, близꙋ̀ положи́ша, во и҆зсѣ́ченомъ ѿ ка́мене гро́бѣ І҆ѡ́сифовѣ, и҆дѣ́же никто́же пре́жде лежа̀, да не Хрⷭ҇тꙋ воскр҃шꙋ, и҆но́мꙋ воскрⷭ҇нїе напи́шꙋти. Смѣше́нїю же а҆лѡ́а и҆ смѵ́рны, припѣча́тительнымъ сꙋ́щымъ, є҆ѵа́ггелъ воспомѧнꙋ̀, да є҆гда̀ ви́дѧтъ плащани́цꙋ и҆ сꙋда́рь, во гро́бѣ ѡ҆ста́влены, не непщꙋ́ютъ ᲂу҆кра́денꙋ є҆мꙋ̀ бы́ти: ка́кѡ бо свободѣ̀ толи́цѣй не сꙋ́щей, ꙗ҆́коже и҆ ѿто́ргнꙋти ѻ҆нал си́це взаждє́ннаѧ пло́ти; Сїа̑ всѧ̑ пресла́внѡ бы́вшаѧ къ тогда́шнее Пѧтка̀ вре́мѧ, и҆ на́мъ си́хъ всѣ́хъ па́мѧть твори́ти, со сокрꙋше́нїемъ се́рдца и҆ ᲂу҆миле́нїемъ, бг҃оно́снїи Ѻ҆ц҃ы̀ повелѣ́ша. Вѣ́домо же ᲂу҆́бѡ, ꙗ҆́кѡ въ шесты́й де́нь седми́цы, ꙗ҆́кѣ въ Пѧто́къ распѧ́тсѧ Гдⷭ҇ь, зане́же и҆ къ шесты́й де́нь и҆знача́ла созда́тисѧ человѣ́кꙋ. Но и҆ къ шесты́й ча́съ днѐ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ повѣ́шенъ бы́сть: занѐ къ то́й ча́съ, ꙗ҆́коже глѧ́тъ, и҆ А҆да́мъ на ѡ҆рече́нное дре́во рꙋ́цѣ просте́ръ косни́сѧ, и҆ ᲂу҆́мре: подоба́ше бо въ ѻ҆́ньже ча́съ сокрꙋше́нъ, въ то́й па́ки созда́тисѧ. Въ вертогра́дѣ же, ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆ А҆да́мъ въ раѝ. Го́рькое питїѐ вкꙋше́нїе ѡ҆бразова́ше. Заꙋше́нїе на́шꙋ свобо́дꙋ ꙗ҆влѧ́ше. Ѻ҆плева́нїе, и҆ безче́стное ѡ҆бхожде́нїе, є҆́же ѡ҆ на́съ че́сти. Терно́вый вѣне́цъ, кла́твы ꙗ҆́же на на́съ ѡ҆гна́нїе. Багрѧ́наѧ ѻ҆де́жда, за кѡ́жаныѧ ри̑зы, и҆ за є҆́же на на́съ црⷭ҇кꙋю ᲂу҆́тварь. Гво́здїе, всеконе́чное на́шегѡ грѣха̀ недвиже́нїе. Крⷭ҇тъ, дре́во є҆́же въ раѝ. Пронзе́наѧ ре́бра А҆да́мово ѡ҆бразова́хꙋ ребро̀, ѿ негѡ́же Є҆́ѵа, ѿ неѧ́же престꙋпле́нїе. Копїѐ, пла́менное ѻ҆рꙋ́жїе мнѣ̀ ѡ҆бхожда́етъ. И҆зъ ре́бръ вода̀, ѻ҆́бразъ кр҃ще́нїа. Кро́вь и҆ тро́сть: и҆́миже на́мъ червле́ными пи́смены, ꙗ҆́кѡ Цр҃ь, дре́внее ѻ҆те́чество дарова̀ и҆ подписа̀. Глаго́летсѧ ᲂу҆́бѡ А҆да́мовѣ главѣ̀ та́мѡ лежа́ти, и҆дѣ́же и҆ Хрⷭ҇то́съ, Глава̀ всѣ́хъ распѧ́тсѧ, кр҃ти́сѧ ᲂу҆́бѡ Хрⷭ҇то́вою Кро́вїю и҆сте́кшею. Ло́бное же мѣ́сто гле́тсѧ, зане́же въ пото́пѣ косте́вшей внѣ̀ землѝ А҆да́мовѣ главѣ̀, ко́сти то́чїю
units.english_text: On Holy and Great Friday we celebrate the holy, saving, and dread Sufferings of our Lord and God and Savior Jesus Christ, which He willingly accepted for our sake: the spittings, the beatings, the blows upon the cheek, the insults, the mockings, the purple garment, the reed, the sponge, the vinegar, the nails, the spear, and after all these, the Cross and death—all of which were accomplished on Friday. For after He was betrayed, having been sold by a friend and disciple for thirty pieces of silver, He was first led unto Annas the high priest, who sent Him unto Caiaphas; where He was spat upon, buffeted on the cheek, and mocked and derided, hearing them say: "Prophesy unto us, O Christ, who is he that struck Thee?" There also false witnesses came forward slandering Him, saying that He said: "Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up"; and that He called Himself the Son of God, whereupon the high priest, unable to bear the blasphemy, tore his clothes. When morning came, He was led unto Pilate in the praetorium; and they went not in, it says, lest they should be defiled, but that they might eat the Passover. For it calls the whole feast the Passover, or it was even then held, as was fitting; but Christ had kept the legal Passover one day before, intending to be sacrificed on Friday. And Pilate going out asked them what accusation they brought against Him; and finding nothing worthy of accusation, he sent Him unto Caiaphas. But they returned again unto Pilate, for they were bent on His murder. And he said: "Take ye Him, and crucify Him, and judge Him according to your law." But they said again: "It is not lawful for us to put any man to death," inciting Pilate to crucify Him. And Pilate asked Christ whether He were the King of the Jews; but He confessed not, but said: "My Kingdom is eternal, not of this world." And Pilate, wishing to release Him, first said unto them that he found in Him no plausible guilt. Then he proposed to release one according to the custom of each feast; but they preferred Barabbas rather than Christ. And Pilate, seeking to gratify the Jews, having first scourged Jesus, brought Him forth with the soldiers, clothed in a scarlet garment, crowned with a crown of thorns, and having a reed placed in His right hand, while the soldiers mocked Him, saying: "Hail, King of the Jews!" Having thus mocked Him to gratify them, Pilate said again: "I find no crime of death in Him." But they said: "Nay, but let us put Him to death, for He calls Himself the Son of God." While these things were spoken, Jesus held His peace; but the people cried unto Pilate: "Crucify, crucify Him!" For they wished to encompass Him with an ignominious death, so that they might blot out even His good memory. But Pilate, as though shaming them, said: "Shall I crucify your King?" And they said that they had no king but Caesar. For having alleged blasphemy and succeeded nothing, they magnified Caesar, that so at least they might fulfill their fury. For they said: "Whosoever makes himself a king makes himself a king, speaks against Caesar." While these things were happening, his wife sent unto Pilate, being terrified by frightening dreams, saying: "Have thou nothing to do with that just Man; for I have suffered many things this night because of Him." And he, being afraid, sought to wash away the guilt of that blood. But they cried out: "His blood be on us and on our children! If thou let this Man go, thou art not Caesar's friend." Pilate, therefore, fearing this, although he well knew Him to be innocent, delivered Him over to the sentence of crucifixion, releasing Barabbas. When Judas saw this, he cast down the pieces of silver and went out, and going away gave himself up to hanging, hanging himself upon a tree; and afterwards, swelling exceedingly, he burst asunder. The soldiers, having mocked Him, beating Him upon the head with a reed, laid the Cross upon Him; then compelling Simon of Cyrene, they laid the Cross upon him to carry it. Being come at the third hour to the Place of the Skull, there they crucified Him, hanging also two other thieves on either side of Him, that He might be numbered as an evildoer. In their greed, the soldiers divided His garments, casting lots for His seamless tunic, committing every excess of insult. Nor was it these things alone, but they mocked Him even while He hung upon the Cross, saying: "Aha, Thou that destroyest the temple and buildest it in three days, save Thyself!" And again: "He saved others, can He not save Himself?" And again: "If He be the King of Israel, let Him now come down from the Cross, and we will believe in Him." And truly, if that cry were sincere, they ought without hesitation to have approached Him; for not only was He acknowledged King of Israel, but of the whole world. For what meant the darkening of the sun for three hours, and that in the middle of the day? That His Passion might be made manifest unto all. And the shaking of the earth, and the rending of the rocks, convicting the hard-heartedness of the Jews; and the bodies of many arising, for the assurance of the general resurrection and for the manifestation of the power of the Sufferer. And the rending of the veil of the temple, as though the temple were indignant at the glorious things suffered by Him Who dwells therein, and revealing the unseen things unto many. At the third hour, then, Christ was crucified, as the divine Mark says; and from the sixth hour until the ninth hour there was darkness, when Longinus the centurion, having seen the most marvelous things, and above all the sun, cried aloud with a great voice: "Truly this was the Son of God!" Of the thieves, indeed, one reviled Jesus, but the other rebuked him with severe reproof, and confessed Christ as the Son of God; and the Savior rewarded his faith, promising him that he should be with Him in paradise. When every insult was fulfilled against Him, Pilate also wrote a title upon Him, saying: "Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews." And though they forbade him to write thus, Pilate replied again: "What I have written, I have written." Then the Savior, having said: "I thirst," they mingled for Him vinegar with gall [sic: vinegar with vinegar]. And having said: "It is finished," He bowed His head and gave up the spirit. When all had departed, His Mother stood by the Cross, and her sister Mary the wife of Cleopas, whom James begat when Cleopas died childless, and also John His beloved disciple. The senseless Jews, not wishing the bodies to remain upon the cross, because it was the great day of the Passover and Friday, besought Pilate that the legs of the condemned might be broken, that death might come more swiftly. And they broke the legs of the others, for they were yet alive; but coming unto Jesus, when they saw that He was dead already, they refrained from breaking them. But one of the soldiers, named Longinus, seeking to please the senseless ones, raised his lance and pierced Christ in His right side; and immediately there came out blood and water: the one as of a man, the other as beyond man; or rather, the blood for the sake of the communion of the divine offerings, and the water for the sake of baptism. For that twofold fountain truly contains the mystery concerning us; and John having seen these things bore witness, and his witness is true, for standing by through all things and seeing them, he writes them: and if he were to speak falsehood, he would not have invented things not existing unto the dishonor of the Master. At that time, it is said, he stood by and received the divine and most holy blood from the life-giving side in a certain vessel. When these things had been accomplished in this supernatural manner, because it was already evening, Joseph who was of Arimathea came forward, a disciple beforehand, hidden even as the others, and coming unto Pilate with boldness, as he was known unto him, asked for the body of Jesus; and he commanded it to be given. And taking it down from the Cross, he laid it with all reverence. And when night had already come, Nicodemus came, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, compounded with cedar, and wrapping it in a shroud, as was the manner of the Jews to bury, they laid it nearby, in a tomb hewn out of stone belonging to Joseph, wherein no man had ever yet been laid, lest when Christ arose, the resurrection should be ascribed to another. And the Gospel mentioned the mixture of aloes and myrrh being adhesive, that when they should see the shroud and the napkin left behind in the tomb, they might not suppose Him to have been stolen away; for how could there have been such leisure as to tear off what was thus glued to the flesh? All these most glorious things having occurred at that Friday time, the God-bearing Fathers commanded us also to make memory of all these things with contrition of heart and compunction. It is to be known, then, that on the sixth day of the week, that is on Friday, the Lord was crucified, because on the sixth day also man was created in the beginning. And in the sixth hour of the day He was hung upon the Cross: for in that hour, as they say, Adam also stretched forth his hands and touched the forbidden tree, and died; for it was fitting that in the same hour wherein he was crushed, he should be created anew. And in a garden, even as Adam was in paradise. The bitter drink prefigured the tasting. The buffeting made manifest our freedom. The spitting and dishonorable treatment, the honor that is for our sake. The crown of thorns, the driving away of the curse that was upon us. The scarlet robe, instead of the coats of skins and for the royal adornment upon us. The nails, the utter immobility of our sin. The Cross, the tree in paradise. The pierced side prefigured Adam's rib, from which Eve came, from whom came the transgression. The lance wards off from me the flaming sword. The water from the side, the image of baptism. The blood and the reed: wherewith, as a King, He granted and signed unto us our ancient homeland in scarlet letters. For it is said that Adam's skull lay there, where Christ the Head of all was crucified, and it was baptized by the Blood of Christ which flowed forth. And it is called the Place of the Skull, because when the skull of Adam was washed out upon the earth in the deluge, the bone alone...

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: носиме быти ко некоему чуду зримому юже соломон
units.slavonic_diplomatic: носи́мѣ бы́ти, ꙗ҆́кѡ нѣ́коемꙋ чꙋ́дꙋ зри́момꙋ, ю҆́же Соломѡ́нъ че́стїю пра́ѻтца, со всѣ́мъ свои́мъ во́инствомъ, ка́менїемъ множа́йшимъ покры̀. Тѣ́мже и҆ мѣ́сто то̀ Лїѳо́стротонъ, сїесть, каменопостла́нное и҆менова́сѧ. Глаго́лютъ ᲂу҆́бѡ ст҃ы́хъ и҆зря́днїи, ѿ преда́нїа и҆мѣ́ти, и҆ самомꙋ̀ А҆да́мꙋ та́мѡ ѿ А҆́гг҃ла погребенꙋ̀ бы́ти. И҆дѣ́же ᲂу҆́бѡ трꙋ́пъ, та́мѡ и҆ ѻ҆ре́лъ прїи́де: Хрⷭ҇то́съ, вѣ́чный Цр҃ь, но́вый А҆да́мъ, ве́тхаго и҆ дре́вомъ па́дшаго А҆да́ма дре́вомъ и҆сцѣлѧ́ѧй, преесте́ственными, и҆ є҆́же ѡ҆ на́съ неизче́тными твои́ми бл҃гоꙋтро́бїѧми, Хрⷭ҇тѐ Бж҃е, поми́лꙋй на́съ, а҆ми́нь.
units.english_cohort_translation: ...was carried about, being seen as a marvelous wonder, which Solomon, out of honor for the forefather, covered with a multitude of stones with all his army. Therefore was that place called Lithostrotos, that is, the Pavement of Stone.[^207] Moreover, the most eminent of the saints say by tradition that Adam himself was buried there by an angel. Where the carcass is, there also the eagle came: Christ the eternal King, the New Adam, healing by the Tree the old Adam who fell by the tree. Through Thy supernatural and boundless compassions toward us, O Christ God, have mercy on us. Amen.[^208]

units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* "Shake off sleep now from your eyelids, O disciples," Thou didst say, O Christ: "and watch in prayer, that ye enter not into temptation, and most of all, Simon! For unto the stronger belongs the greater trial; understand Me, O Peter: Whom all creation blesses, glorifying Him unto all ages!"

units.slavonic_diplomatic: [В] Скве́рна сло́ва ᲂу҆сте́нъ никогда́же и҆зрекꙋ̀ тебѣ̀ Влⷣко, съ тобо́ю ᲂу҆мрꙋ̀ ꙗ҆́кѡ бл҃горазꙋ́менъ, а҆́ще и҆ всѝ ѿве́ргꙋтсѧ, возопѝ Пе́тръ, ни пло́ть, нижѐ кро́вь, но Ѻ҆ц҃ъ тво́й ѿкры́ ми тѧ̀: є҆го́же всѧ̀ тва́рь бл҃гослови́тъ, сла́вѧщи во вѣ́ки.

units.slavonic_incipit: Глꙋбинꙋ̀ премꙋ́дрости бж҃твенныѧ и҆ ра́зꙋма не
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: глубину премудрости бжтвенныя и разума не всю испытал
units.slavonic_diplomatic: [В] Глꙋбинꙋ̀ премꙋ́дрости бж҃твенныѧ и҆ ра́зꙋма не всю̀ и҆спыта́лъ є҆сѝ, бе́зднꙋ же мои́хъ сꙋде́бъ не пости́глъ є҆сѝ человѣ́че, Гдⷭ҇ь речѐ: пло́ть ᲂу҆́бѡ сы́й, не хвали́сѧ: три́жды бо ѿве́ржешисѧ менѐ: є҆го́же всѧ̀ тва́рь бл҃гослови́тъ, сла́вѧщи во вѣ́ки.
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion:* "The depth of divine wisdom and understanding hast thou not fully searched out, and the abyss of My judgments hast thou not comprehended, O man," the Lord said: "being therefore flesh, boast not; for thrice shalt thou deny Me: Whom all creation blesses, glorifying Him unto all ages!"

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: ирмос т чтнейшую херувим и славнейшую без сравнения

units.slavonic_incipit: Два̀ и҆ лꙋка̑внаѧ сотворѝ перворожде́нный сы́нъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: два и лукавная сотвори перворожденный сын мой иил
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Два̀ и҆ лꙋка̑внаѧ сотворѝ перворожде́нный сы́нъ мо́й І҆и҃ль: менѐ ѡ҆ста́ви, И҆сто́чника воды̀ живо́тныѧ, и҆ и҆скопа̀ себѣ̀ кладе́нѧзъ сокрꙋше́нный: менѐ на дре́вѣ распѧ́тъ, Вара́ввꙋ же и҆спросѝ, и҆ ѿпꙋстѝ, ᲂу҆жасе́сѧ нб҃о ѡ҆ се́мъ, и҆ со́лнце лꙋчѝ скры̀: ты́ же І҆и҃лю не ᲂу҆срами́лсѧ є҆сѝ, но сме́рти мѧ̀ пре́далъ є҆сѝ, ѡ҆ста́ви и҆̀мъ, Ѻ҆́ч҃е Ст҃ы́й, не вѣ́дѧтъ бо, что̀ сотвори́ша.
units.english_cohort_translation: Two evils hath My firstborn son Israel committed: he hath forsaken Me, the Fountain of living water, and hewn out for himself a broken cistern; Me hath he crucified upon the tree, but Barabbas he begged and released; heaven was appalled at this, and the sun hid its beams: but thou, O Israel, wast not ashamed, but didst deliver Me over unto death; forgive them, O Holy Father, for they know not what they have done!

units.slavonic_incipit: Кі́йждо ᲂу҆́дъ ст҃ы́ѧ твоеѧ̀ Пло́ти, безче́стїе
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: кийждо уд стыя твоея плоти безчестие нас ради
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Кі́йждо ᲂу҆́дъ ст҃ы́ѧ твоеѧ̀ Пло́ти, безче́стїе на́съ ра́ди претерпѣ̀: те́рнїе, глава̀: лицѐ, ѡ҆плева́нїа: че́люсти, заꙋше́нїа: ᲂу҆ста̀, во ѻ҆́цтѣ растворе́ннꙋю же́лчь вкꙋ́сомъ: ᲂу҆шеса̀, хꙋле́нїа ѕлочести̑ваѧ: плещѝ, бїе́нїа: и҆ рꙋка̀, тро́сть: всегѡ̀ Тѣлесѐ протѧже́нїа на крⷭ҇тѣ̀: чле́нове, гвѡ́здїа: и҆ рє́бра, копїѐ. Пострада́вый за ны̀, и҆ ѿ страсте́й свободи́вый на́съ, снизше́дый къ на́мъ человѣ́колю́бїемъ, и҆ вознесы́й на́съ, всеси́льне Сп҃се, поми́лꙋй на́съ.
units.english_cohort_translation: Every member of Thy holy Flesh endured dishonor for our sake: the head, the thorns; the face, the spittings; the cheeks, the buffeting; the mouth, the tasting of gall mingled with vinegar; the ears, the impious blasphemies; the shoulders, the scourgings; and the hand, the reed; the stretching of the whole Body upon the Cross; the limbs, the nails; and the side, the lance. O Thou Who didst suffer for us and free us from passions, Who didst condescend unto us in Thy love for mankind and raise us up: O all-powerful Savior, have mercy on us!

units.slavonic_incipit: Распе́ншꙋся тѝ Хрⷭ҇тѐ, всѧ̀ тва́рь ви́дѧщи
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: распеншуся ти хрт вся твар видящи трепеташе основаниа
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Распе́ншꙋся тѝ Хрⷭ҇тѐ, всѧ̀ тва́рь ви́дѧщи трепета́ше, ѡ҆снова̑нїа землѝ позыба́шася стра́хомъ держа́вы твоеѧ̀: тебѣ́ бо возне́сшꙋся дне́сь, ро́дъ є҆вре́йскїй поги́бе, цр҃ко́внаѧ завѣ́са раздра́сѧ на дво́е, и҆ ме́ртвїи ѿ гро́бѡвъ воскресо́ша, со́тникъ ви́дѣвъ чꙋ́до, ᲂу҆жасе́сѧ, предстоѧ́щи же Мт҃и твоѧ̀ вопїѧ́ше, рыда́ющи мт҃рски: ка́кѡ не возрыда́ю, и҆ ᲂу҆тро́бы моеѧ̀ не бїю̀, зрѧ́щи тѧ̀ на́га, ꙗ҆́кѡ ѡ҆сꙋжде́на, на дре́вѣ ви́сѧща; распны́йсѧ и҆ погребы́йсѧ, и҆ воскресы́й и҆зъ ме́ртвыхъ, Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ̀.
units.english_cohort_translation: When Thou wast crucified, O Christ, all creation trembled beholding it; the foundations of the earth were shaken for fear of Thy dominion; for when Thou wast lifted up today, the Hebrew race perished; the veil of the temple was torn in twain, and the dead arose from their tombs; the centurion, having seen the miracle, was terrified; and Thy Mother who stood by cried aloud, lamenting with motherly grief: "How shall I not wail, and how shall I not beat my breast, beholding Thee naked, as one condemned, hanging upon the Tree? O Thou Who wast crucified, and buried, and didst rise from the dead: O Lord, glory be to Thee!"

...today, the Hebrew race perished; the veil of the temple was torn in twain, and the dead arose from their tombs; the centurion, having seen the miracle, was terrified; and Thy Mother who stood by cried aloud, lamenting with motherly grief: "How shall I not wail, and how shall I not beat my breast, beholding Thee naked, as one condemned, hanging upon the Tree? O Thou Who wast crucified, and buried, and didst rise from the dead: O Lord, glory be to Thee!"

units.slavonic_incipit: Всѧ̀ тва́рь и҆змѣнѧ́шеся стра́хомъ, зрѧ́щи тѧ̀
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: вся твар изменяшеся страхом зрящи тя на крте
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Всѧ̀ тва́рь и҆змѣнѧ́шеся стра́хомъ, зрѧ́щи тѧ̀ на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ ви́сима Хрⷭ҇тѐ, со́лнце ѡ҆мрача́шеся, и҆ землѝ ѡ҆снова̑нїа сотрѧса́хꙋся, всѧ̑ сострада́хꙋ Созда́вшемꙋ всѧ̑, во́лею на́съ ра́ди претерпѣ́вый, Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ̀.
units.english_cohort_translation: All creation was transformed by fear, beholding Thee hanging upon the Cross, O Christ; the sun was darkened, and the foundations of the earth were shaken; all things suffered with the Creator of all: O Thou Who willingly didst endure for our sake, O Lord, glory be to Thee!

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Лю́дїе ѕлочести́вїи и҆ беззако́ннїи, вскꙋ́ю поꙋча́ютсѧ тще́тнымъ; вскꙋ́ю Живота̀ всѣ́хъ на сме́рть ѡ҆сꙋди́ша; ве́лїе чꙋ́до, ꙗ҆́кѡ Созда́тель мі́ра въ рꙋ́ки беззако́нныхъ предае́тсѧ, и҆ на дре́во возвыша́етсѧ Человѣ́колю́бецъ, да и҆̀же во а҆́дѣ ᲂу҆́зники свободи́тъ зовꙋ́щыѧ: долготерпѣли́ве Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ̀.
units.english_cohort_translation: O people impious and lawless, why do ye meditate on vain things? Why did ye condemn the Life of all unto death? A great marvel it is that the Creator of the world is delivered into the hands of the lawless, and the Lover of mankind is lifted up upon the tree, that He may free the prisoners in Hades who cry: O long-suffering Lord, glory be to Thee!

units.slavonic_incipit: Дне́сь зрѧ́щи тѧ̀ непоро́чнаѧ Дв҃а на
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: днес зрящи тя непорочная два на крте слове
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Дне́сь зрѧ́щи тѧ̀ непоро́чнаѧ Дв҃а на крⷭ҇тѣ̀, Сло́ве, возвыша́ема, рыда́ющи мт҃рнею ᲂу҆тро́бою, ᲂу҆ѧзвля́шеся се́рдцемъ го́рцѣ, и҆ стена́ющи болѣ́зненнѡ и҆зъ глꙋбины̀ дꙋшѝ, лицѐ со власы̀ терза́ющи, тѣ́мже и҆ пе́рси бїю́щи, взыва́ше жа́лостнѡ: ᲂу҆вы́ мнѣ̀, бж҃е́ственное Ча́до! ᲂу҆вы́ мнѣ̀, Свѣ́те мі́ра! что̀ заше́лъ є҆сѝ ѿ ѻ҆́чїю мое́ю, А҆́гнче Бж҃їй; тѣ́мже вѡ́инства безпло́тныхъ, тре́петомъ содержи́ми бя́хꙋ, глаго́люще: непостижи́ме Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ̀.
units.english_cohort_translation: Today the spotless Virgin, beholding Thee lifted up upon the Cross, O Word, weeping with a mother's heart, was bitterly wounded in spirit, and groaning in anguish from the depth of her soul, tearing her face and hair and beating her breast, cried out piteously: "Woe is me, my divine Child! Woe is me, Light of the world! Why hast Thou set from mine eyes, O Lamb of God?" Therefore the hosts of the bodiless powers were held with trembling, saying: O incomprehensible Lord, glory be to Thee!

units.slavonic_incipit: На дре́вѣ ви́дѧщи ви́сима Хрⷭ҇тѐ, тебѐ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: на древе видящи висима хрт теб всех зиждителя
units.slavonic_diplomatic: На дре́вѣ ви́дѧщи ви́сима Хрⷭ҇тѐ, тебѐ всѣ́хъ Зижди́телѧ и҆ Бг҃а, безсѣ́меннѡ Ро́ждшаѧ тѧ̀, вопїѧ́ше го́рькѡ: Сн҃е мо́й, гдѣ̀ добро́та за́йде зра́ка твоегѡ̀; не терплю̀ зрѣ́ти тѧ̀ непра́веднѡ распина́ема: потщи́ся ᲂу҆́бо, воста́ни, ꙗ҆́кѡ да ви́ждꙋ и҆ а҆́зъ твоѐ и҆зъ ме́ртвыхъ тридне́вное Воскрⷭ҇нїе.
units.english_cohort_translation: Beholding Thee hanging upon the tree, O Christ, the Creator and God of all, She that bare Thee without seed cried bitterly: "O my Son, whither hath the beauty of Thine appearance set? I cannot bear to behold Thee unrighteously crucified; hasten therefore, arise, that I also may see Thy third-day Resurrection from the dead!"

units.slavonic_incipit: Гдⷭ҇и, восходѧ́щꙋ тѝ на крⷭ҇тъ, стра́хъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: гди восходящу ти на крт страх и трепет
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Гдⷭ҇и, восходѧ́щꙋ тѝ на крⷭ҇тъ, стра́хъ и҆ тре́петъ нападѐ на тва́рь, и҆ землѝ ᲂу҆́бѡ возбраня́лъ є҆сѝ поглоти́ти распина́ющихъ тѧ̀, а҆́дꙋ же повелѣва́лъ є҆сѝ и҆спꙋсти́ти ᲂу҆́зники, на ѡ҆бновле́нїе человѣ́кѡвъ, Сꙋдїѐ живы́хъ и҆ ме́ртвыхъ, жи́знь прише́лъ є҆сѝ пода́ти, а҆ не сме́рть: Чл҃вѣколю́бче сла́ва тебѣ̀.
units.english_cohort_translation: O Lord, when Thou didst ascend upon the Cross, fear and trembling fell upon creation, and Thou didst forbid the earth to swallow up them that crucified Thee, and unto Hades Thou didst command to yield up its prisoners for the renewal of men, O Judge of the living and the dead, Who camest to bestow life and not death: O Lover of mankind, glory be to Thee!
units.slavonic_text: Гдⷭ҇и, восходѧ́щꙋ тѝ на крⷭ҇тъ, стра́хъ и҆ тре́петъ нападѐ на тва́рь, и҆ землѝ ᲂу҆́бѡ возбраня́лъ є҆сѝ поглоти́ти распина́ющихъ тѧ̀, а҆́дꙋ же повелѣва́лъ є҆сѝ и҆спꙋсти́ти ᲂу҆́зники, на ѡ҆бновле́нїе человѣ́кѡвъ, Сꙋдїѐ живы́хъ и҆ ме́ртвыхъ, жи́знь прише́лъ є҆сѝ пода́ти, а҆ не сме́рть: Чл҃вѣколю́бче сла́ва тебѣ̀.
units.english_text: O Lord, when Thou didst ascend upon the Cross, fear and trembling fell upon creation, and Thou didst forbid the earth to swallow up them that crucified Thee, and unto Hades Thou didst command to yield up its prisoners for the renewal of men, O Judge of the living and the dead, Who camest to bestow life and not death: O Lover of mankind, glory be to Thee!

units.slavonic_incipit: Оу҆жѐ ѡ҆мака́етсѧ тро́сть и҆зрече́нїа: ѿ сꙋде́й
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: оуж омакается трост изречениа от судей неправедных иис
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Оу҆жѐ ѡ҆мака́етсѧ тро́сть и҆зрече́нїа: ѿ сꙋде́й непра́ведныхъ, І҆и҃съ сꙋди́мъ быва́етъ, и҆ ѡ҆сꙋжда́етсѧ на крⷭ҇тъ, и҆ стра́ждетъ тва́рь, на крⷭ҇тѣ̀ ви́дѧщи Гдⷭ҇а: но є҆стество́мъ тѣ́лесѐ, менѐ ра́ди стражда́й Бл҃гі́й, Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ̀.
units.english_cohort_translation: *Troparion, Tone 4:*[^218] Thou hast redeemed us from the curse of the Law by Thy precious Blood, having been nailed unto the Cross and pierced with a lance: Thou hast poured forth immortality unto men, O our Savior, glory be to Thee!

units.slavonic_incipit: Глаго́лы моѧ̑ внꙋшѝ Гдⷭ҇и, разꙋмѣ́й зва́нїе
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: глаголы моя внуши гди разумей звание мо вонми
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Глаго́лы моѧ̑ внꙋшѝ Гдⷭ҇и, разꙋмѣ́й зва́нїе моѐ. Вонмѝ гла́сꙋ моле́нїѧ моегѡ̀, Цр҃ю̀ мо́й и҆ Бж҃е мо́й, ꙗ҆́кѡ къ тебѣ̀ помолю́сѧ Гдⷭ҇и. Заꙋ́тра ᲂу҆слы́ши гла́съ мо́й, заꙋ́тра предста́нꙋ тѝ, и҆ ᲂу҆́зриши мѧ̀. Ꙗ҆́кѡ Бг҃ъ не хотѧ́й беззако́нїѧ, ты́ є҆си: не присели́тсѧ къ тебѣ̀ лꙋка́внꙋѧй. Нижѐ пребꙋ́дꙋтъ беззако́нницы пред̾ ѻ҆чи́ма твои́ма, возненави́дѣлъ є҆сѝ всѧ̑ дѣ́лающыѧ беззако́нїе. Погꙋби́ши всѧ̑ глаго́лющыѧ лжꙋ̀, мꙋ́жа крове́й и҆ льсти́ва гнꙋша́етсѧ Гдⷭ҇ь. А҆́зъ же мно́жествомъ ми́лости твоеѧ̀, вни́дꙋ въ до́мъ тво́й, поклоню́сѧ ко хра́мꙋ ст҃о́мꙋ твоемꙋ̀, въ стра́сѣ твое́мъ, Гдⷭ҇и наста́ви мѧ̀ пра́вдою твое́ю, вра̑гъ мои́хъ ра́ди и҆спра́ви пред̾ тобо́ю пꙋ́ть мо́й. Ꙗ҆́кѡ нѣ́сть во ᲂу҆стнѣ́хъ и҆́хъ и҆́стины, се́рдце и҆́хъ сꙋ́етно, гро́бъ ѿве́рстъ горта́нь и҆́хъ, ѧ҆зы́ки свои́ми льща́хꙋ. Сꙋдѝ и҆̀мъ Бж҃е, да ѿпа́дꙋтъ ѿ мы́слей свои́хъ, по мно́жествꙋ нече́стїѧ и҆́хъ и҆зри́ни ѧ҆̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ преѡгорчи́ша тѧ̀ Гдⷭ҇и. И҆ да возвесе́лѧтсѧ всѝ ᲂу҆пова́ющїи на тѧ̀, во вѣ́къ возра́дꙋютсѧ, и҆ всели́шисѧ въ ни́хъ, и҆ похва́лѧтсѧ ѡ҆ тебѣ̀ любѧ́щїи и҆́мѧ твоѐ. Ꙗ҆́кѡ ты̀ бл҃гослови́ши пра́ведника Гдⷭ҇и, ꙗ҆́кѡ ѻ҆рꙋ́жїемъ бл҃говоле́нїѧ вѣнча́лъ є҆сѝ на́съ.
units.english_cohort_translation: Give ear to my words, O Lord, consider my cry. Attend unto the voice of my supplication, my King and my God, for unto Thee will I pray, O Lord. In the morning Thou shalt hear my voice; in the morning I will stand before Thee, and Thou shalt look upon me. For Thou art not a God that desirest iniquity; the worker of evil shall not dwell with Thee. Neither shall transgressors abide before Thine eyes; Thou hast hated all them that work iniquity. Thou shalt destroy all them that speak a lie; the man of blood and deceit the Lord abhorrs. But as for me, in the multitude of Thy mercy I will enter into Thy house; I will worship toward Thy holy temple in Thy fear. Lead me, O Lord, in Thy righteousness; because of mine enemies, make straight my way before Thee. For there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain; their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have dealt deceitfully. Judge them, O God; let them fall from their counsels; according to the multitude of their impieties cast them out, for they have embittered Thee, O Lord. And let all them that hope in Thee be glad; they shall rejoice for ever, and Thou shalt dwell in them; and they that love Thy name shall boast in Thee. For Thou shalt bless the righteous, O Lord; Thou hast crowned us as with a shield of good pleasure.

Thou shalt destroy all them that speak a lie; the man of blood and deceit the Lord abhorrs. But as for me, in the multitude of Thy mercy I will enter into Thy house; I will worship toward Thy holy temple in Thy fear. Lead me, O Lord, in Thy righteousness; because of mine enemies, make straight my way before Thee. For there is no truth in their mouth; their heart is vain; their throat is an open sepulchre; with their tongues they have dealt deceitfully. Judge them, O God; let them fall from their counsels; according to the multitude of their impieties cast them out, for they have embittered Thee, O Lord. And let all them that hope in Thee be glad; they shall rejoice for ever, and Thou shalt dwell in them; and they that love Thy name shall boast

units.slavonic_stem_tier2: вскую шаташася зыцы и людие поучишася тщетным предсташа
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Вскꙋ́ю шата́шасѧ ꙗ҆зы́цы, и҆ лю́дїе поꙋчи́шасѧ тщє́тнымъ; Предста́ша ца́рїе зе́мстїи, и҆ кнѧ̑зи собра́шасѧ вкꙋ́пѣ на Гдⷭ҇а и҆ на Хрⷭ҇та̀ є҆гѡ̀: Расто́ргнемъ ᲂу҆́зы и҆́хъ, и҆ ѿве́ржемъ ѿ на́съ и҆́го и҆́хъ. Живы́й на небесѣ́хъ посмѣе́тсѧ и҆̀мъ, и҆ Гдⷭ҇ь порꙋга́етсѧ и҆̀мъ. Тогда̀ возгла́етъ къ ни́мъ гнѣ́вомъ свои́мъ, и҆ ꙗ҆́ростїю свое́ю смѧте́тъ ѧ҆̀. А҆́зъ же поста́вленъ є҆́смь Цр҃ь ѿ негѡ̀ на́дъ Сїѡ́номъ горо́ю ст҃о́ю є҆гѡ̀, возвѣща́ѧй повелѣ́нїе Гдⷭ҇не, Гдⷭ҇ь речѐ ко мнѣ̀: Сы́нъ мо́й є҆сѝ ты̀, а҆́зъ дне́сь роди́хъ тѧ̀. Просѝ ѿ менѐ, и҆ да́мъ тѝ ꙗ҆зы́ки достоѧ́нїе твоѐ, и҆ ᲂу҆держа́нїе твоѐ концы̀ землѝ. Оу҆пасе́ши ѧ҆̀ жезло́мъ желѣ́знымъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ сосꙋ́ды скꙋде́льничи сокрꙋши́ши ѧ҆̀. И҆ ны́нѣ ца́рїе разꙋмѣ́йте, накажи́тесѧ всѝ сꙋдѧ́щїи землѝ. Рабо́тайте Гдⷭ҇ви со стра́хомъ, и҆ ра́дꙋйтесѧ є҆мꙋ̀ съ тре́петомъ. Прїими́те наказа́нїе, да не когда̀ прогнѣ́ваетсѧ Гдⷭ҇ь, и҆ поги́бнете ѿ пꙋтѝ пра́веднагѡ, є҆гда̀ возгори́тсѧ вско́рѣ ꙗ҆́рость є҆гѡ̀. Бл҃же́ни всѝ надѣ́ющїисѧ на́нь.
units.english_cohort_translation: Why have the heathen raged, and the peoples meditated on vain things? The kings of the earth stood up, and the rulers gathered together, against the Lord and against His Anointed: "Let us break their bonds asunder, and cast away their yoke from us!" He that dwells in the heavens shall laugh them to scorn, and the Lord shall deride them. Then shall He speak unto them in His wrath, and in His fury shall He trouble them. But as for Me, I was established King by Him upon Zion His holy mountain, proclaiming the commandment of the Lord. The Lord said unto Me: "Thou art My Son, this day have I begotten Thee. Ask of Me, and I will give Thee the nations for Thine inheritance, and the ends of the earth for Thy possession. Thou shalt shepherd them with a rod of iron; as a potter's vessels shalt Thou shatter them." And now, O ye kings, understand; receive instruction, all ye that judge the earth. Serve the Lord with fear, and rejoice in Him with trembling. Accept instruction, lest the Lord be angry, and ye perish from the righteous way, when His wrath is kindled in a moment. Blessed are all they that put their trust in Him.

units.slavonic_incipit: Бж҃е, Бж҃е мо́й, вонми́ ми, вскꙋ́ю
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: бже бже мой вонми ми вскую оставил мя
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Бж҃е, Бж҃е мо́й, вонми́ ми, вскꙋ́ю ѡ҆ста́вилъ мѧ̀ є҆сѝ; дале́че ѿ спасе́нїѧ моегѡ̀ словеса̀ грѣхопаде́нїй мои́хъ. Бж҃е мо́й, воззовꙋ̀ ко днѝ и҆ не ᲂу҆слы́шиши, и҆ въ нощѝ, и҆ не въ безꙋ́мїе мнѣ̀. Ты́ же во ст҃ы́хъ живе́ши, Хвало̀ І҆и҃лева. На тѧ̀ ᲂу҆пова́ша ѻ҆тцы̀ на́ши, ᲂу҆пова́ша, и҆ и҆зба́вилъ є҆сѝ ѧ҆̀. Къ тебѣ̀ воззва́ша, и҆ спасо́шасѧ: на тѧ̀ ᲂу҆пова́ша, и҆ не постыдѣ́шасѧ. А҆́зъ же є҆́смь че́рвь, а҆ не человѣ́къ, поноше́нїе человѣ́кѡвъ, и҆ ᲂу҆ничиже́нїе люде́й. Всѝ ви́дѧщїи мѧ̀ порꙋга́шамисѧ, глаго́лаша ᲂу҆стна́ми, покива́ша главо́ю. Оу҆пова̀ на Гдⷭ҇а, да и҆зба́витъ є҆го̀, да спасе́тъ є҆го̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ хо́щетъ є҆го̀. Ꙗ҆́кѡ ты̀ є҆сѝ и҆сто́ргїй мѧ̀ и҆з̾ чре́ва: ᲂу҆пова́нїе моѐ ѿ сосцꙋ̑ ма́тере моеѧ̀. Къ тебѣ̀ приверженъ є҆́смь ѿ ложе́снъ, ѿ чре́ва ма́тере моеѧ̀, Бг҃ъ мо́й є҆сѝ ты̀. Да не ѡ҆тстꙋ́пиши ѿ менѐ: ꙗ҆́кѡ ско́рбь бли́зъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ нѣ́сть помога́ѧй мѝ. Ѡ҆быдо́ша мѧ̀ тельцы̀ мно́зи, ю҆нцы̀ тꙋ́чнїи ѡ҆держа́ша мѧ̀. Ѿверзо́ша на мѧ̀ ᲂу҆ста̀ своѧ̑, ꙗ҆́кѡ ле́въ восхища́ѧй и҆ рыка́ѧй. Ꙗ҆́кѡ вода̀ и҆злїѧ́хсѧ, и҆ разсы́пашасѧ всѧ̑ кѡ́сти моѧ̑: бы́сть се́рдце моѐ, ꙗ҆́кѡ во́скъ та́ѧй посредѣ̀ чре́ва моегѡ̀. И҆зсше ꙗ҆́кѡ скꙋде́ль крѣ́пость моѧ̀, и҆ ѧ҆зы́къ мо́й прильпѐ горта́ни моемꙋ̀, и҆ въ пе́рсть сме́рти све́лъ мѧ̀ є҆сѝ. Ꙗ҆́кѡ ѡ҆быдо́ша мѧ̀ псѝ мно́зи, со́нмъ лꙋка́выхъ ѡ҆держа́ша мѧ̀. И҆скопа́ша рꙋ́цѣ моѝ и҆ но́зѣ моѝ. И҆счето́ша всѧ̑ кѡ́сти моѧ̑, ті́и же смотри́ша, и҆ презрѣ́ша мѧ̀. Раздѣли́ша ри̑зы моѧ̑ себѣ̀, и҆ ѡ҆ ѻ҆де́жди мое́й мета́ша жре́бїй. Ты́ же Гдⷭ҇и не ᲂу҆далѝ по́мощь твою̀ ѿ менѐ, на застꙋпле́нїе моѐ вонмѝ. И҆зба́ви ѿ ѻ҆рꙋ́жїѧ дꙋ́шꙋ мою̀, и҆ и҆з̾ рꙋкѝ пе́сїи є҆диноро́днꙋю мою̀. Спаси́ мѧ ѿ ᲂу҆́стъ льво́выхъ, и҆ ѿ рѡ́гъ є҆динорѡ́жъ смире́нїе моѐ. Повѣ́мъ и҆́мѧ твоѐ бра́тїи мое́й, посредѣ̀ Це́ркве воспою́ тѧ. Боѧ́щїисѧ Гдⷭ҇а восхвали́те є҆го̀, всѐ сѣ́мѧ І҆а́кѡвле просла́вите є҆го̀. Да ᲂу҆бои́тсѧ же ѿ негѡ̀ всѐ сѣ́мѧ І҆и҃лево: Ꙗ҆́кѡ не ᲂу҆ничижѝ, нижѐ негодова̀ мл҃твы ни́щагѡ, нижѐ ѿвратѝ лицѐ своѐ ѿ менѐ: и҆ є҆гда̀ воззва́хъ къ немꙋ̀, ᲂу҆слы́ша мѧ̀. Ѿ тебѐ похвала̀ моѧ̀, въ Це́ркви вели́цѣй и҆сповѣ́мсѧ тебѣ̀. Моли́твы моѧ̑ возда́мъ пред̾ боѧ́щимисѧ є҆гѡ̀: Ꙗ҆дѧ́тъ ᲂу҆бо́зїи, и҆ насы́тѧтсѧ, и҆ восхва́лѧтъ Гдⷭ҇а взыска́ющїи є҆го̀, жива̀ бꙋ́дꙋтъ сердца̀ и҆́хъ въ вѣ́къ вѣ́ка. Помянꙋ́тсѧ и҆ ѡ҆братѧ́тсѧ ко Гдⷭ҇ꙋ всѝ концы̀ землѝ, и҆ покло́нѧтсѧ пред̾ ни́мъ всѧ̑ ѻ҆те́чествїѧ ꙗ҆зы́къ. Ꙗ҆́кѡ Гдⷭ҇не є҆́сть Црⷭ҇твїе, и҆ то́й ѡ҆блада́етъ ꙗ҆зы́ки. Ꙗ҆до́ша и҆ поклони́шасѧ всѝ тꙋ́чнїи землѝ, пред̾ ни́мъ припа́дꙋтъ всѝ низходѧ́щїи въ зе́млю, и҆ дꙋша̀ моѧ̀ томꙋ̀ живе́тъ: И҆ сѣ́мѧ моѐ порабѡ́таетъ є҆мꙋ̀, возвѣсти́тъ Гдⷭ҇ви ро́дъ грѧдꙋ́щїй. И҆ возвѣстѧ́тъ пра́вдꙋ є҆гѡ̀ лю́демъ ро́ждшымсѧ, ꙗ҆̀же сотворѝ Гдⷭ҇ь.
units.english_cohort_translation: O God, my God, attend unto me; why hast Thou forsaken me? Far from my salvation are the words of my transgressions. O my God, I will cry by day, and Thou wilt not hear; and by night, and it shall not be accounted folly unto me. But Thou dwellest in the holy place, O Thou Praise of Israel. In Thee our fathers hoped; they hoped, and Thou didst deliver them. Unto Thee they cried, and they were saved; in Thee they hoped, and were not put to shame. But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and an outcast of the people. All they that saw me laughed me to scorn; they spoke with their lips, they shook the head: "He hoped in the Lord, let Him deliver him; let Him save him, since He desires him." For Thou art He that drew me out of the womb, my hope from my mother's breasts. Upon Thee was I cast from the womb; from my mother's belly, Thou art my God. Depart not from me, for tribulation is nigh, for there is none to help. Many bullocks have compassed me; fat bulls have beset me round. They opened their mouth against me, as a ravening and roaring lion. I am poured out like water, and all my bones are scattered; my heart is become like wax melting in the midst of my belly. My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue hath cleaved to my jaws, and into the dust of death hast Thou brought me down. For many dogs have compassed me; the assembly of the wicked hath enclosed me. They pierced my hands and my feet. They numbered all my bones, and they looked and stared upon me. They parted my garments among them, and upon my vesture they cast lots. But Thou, O Lord, remove not Thy help far from me; attend unto my defense. Deliver my soul from the sword, and mine only-begotten from the paw of the dog. Save me from the lion's mouth, and my lowliness from the horns of the unicorns. I will declare Thy name unto my brethren; in the midst of the Church will I hymn Thee. Ye that fear the Lord, praise Him; all ye seed of Jacob, glorify Him. Let all the seed of Israel fear Him. For He hath not despised nor abhorred the supplication of the poor, neither hath He turned away His face from me; and when I cried unto Him, He heard me. From Thee is my praise; in the great Church will I confess Thee; I will pay my vows before them that fear Him. The poor shall eat and be satisfied, and they that seek the Lord shall praise Him; their hearts shall live unto ages of ages. All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn unto the Lord, and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before Him. For the kingdom is the Lord's, and He rules over the nations. All the fat ones of the earth have eaten and worshipped; all they that go down into the earth shall fall down before Him; and my soul lives unto Him. And my seed shall serve Him; the generation that comes shall be declared unto the Lord. And they shall declare His righteousness unto a people that shall be born, whom the Lord hath made.

units.slavonic_incipit: Распе́ншꙋсѧ тебѣ̀ Хрⷭ҇тѐ, поги́бе мꙋчи́тельство, попра́на

units.slavonic_diplomatic: Распе́ншꙋсѧ тебѣ̀ Хрⷭ҇тѐ, поги́бе мꙋчи́тельство, попра́на бы́сть си́ла вра́жїѧ: нижѐ бо а҆́гг҃лъ, нижѐ человѣ́къ, но са́мъ Гдⷭ҇и спа́слъ є҆сѝ на́съ, сла́ва тебѣ̀.

units.slavonic_incipit: Что́ тѧ нарече́мъ: ѽ Ѽбра́дованнаѧ; Не́бо;
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: что тя наречем брадованная небо ко возсияла
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Что́ тѧ нарече́мъ: ѽ Ѽбра́дованнаѧ; Не́бо; ꙗ҆́кѡ возсїѧ́ла є҆сѝ Сл҃нце пра́вды. Ра́й; ꙗ҆́кѡ возрасти́ла є҆сѝ Цвѣ́тъ нетлѣ́нїѧ. Дв҃ꙋ; ꙗ҆́кѡ пребыла̀ є҆сѝ нетлѣ́нна. Чтⷭ҇ꙋю Мт҃рь; ꙗ҆́кѡ и҆мѣ́ла є҆сѝ на рꙋкꙋ̑ Сн҃а, всѣ́хъ Бг҃а, того̀ молѝ, спасти́сѧ дꙋша́мъ на́шымъ.
units.english_cohort_translation: What shall we call thee, O thou full of grace? Heaven, for thou hast made the Sun of righteousness to shine forth; Paradise, for thou hast blossomed the Flower of incorruption; Virgin, for thou hast remained undefiled; Pure Mother, for thou hast held in thy holy arms a Son, the God of all: Him do thou entreat, that our souls may be saved.

units.slavonic_incipit: Та́же пое́мъ тропарѝ трѝ ѿ двѣна́десѧти,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: таже поем тропари три от двенадесяти повторяюще я
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Та́же пое́мъ тропарѝ трѝ ѿ двѣна́десѧти, повторѧ́юще ѧ҆̀: глаго́лемъ же пе́рвый без̾ стїха̀, та́кѡ бо твори́мъ и҆ въ про́чихъ Часѣ́хъ къ пе́рвый тропа́рь. Во вторы́й же, пое́тъ нача́ншїй ли́къ сті́хъ, и҆ пое́тъ и҆̀, та́же па́ки дрꙋгі́й ли́къ сті́хъ, и҆ пое́тъ и҆ то́й и҆̀, тре́тїй же глаго́лемъ на Сла́вꙋ, и҆ на И҆ ны́нѣ.
units.english_cohort_translation: *Then we sing three troparia from the twelve, repeating them: and we say the first without a verse, for so we do also in the other Hours at the first troparion. At the second, the choir that began sings the verse, and sings the troparion; then again the other choir sings the verse, and sings the troparion; and the third we say at Glory, and at Both now.*[^227]

units.slavonic_incipit: Ꙗ҆́кѡ ѻ҆вча̀ на заколе́нїе веде́нъ бы́лъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: ко вча на заколение веден был еси хрт
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Ꙗ҆́кѡ ѻ҆вча̀ на заколе́нїе веде́нъ бы́лъ є҆сѝ Хрⷭ҇тѐ Цр҃ю̀, и҆ ꙗ҆́кѡ а҆́гнецъ неѕло́бивый пригвозди́лсѧ є҆сѝ крⷭ҇тꙋ̀, ѿ беззако́нныхъ мꙋже́й, грѣ̑хъ ра́ди на́шихъ, Человѣколю́бче.
units.english_cohort_translation: As a sheep to the slaughter Thou wast led, O Christ the King, and as an innocent lamb Thou wast nailed to the Cross by lawless men, for our sins, O Lover of mankind.

units.slavonic_incipit: Є҆́мшымъ тѧ̀ беззако́ннымъ, претерпѣва́ѧ, си́це вопїѧ́лъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: емшым тя беззаконным претерпевая сице вопиял еси гди
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Є҆́мшымъ тѧ̀ беззако́ннымъ, претерпѣва́ѧ, си́це вопїѧ́лъ є҆сѝ Гдⷭ҇и: А҆́ще и҆ порази́сте Па́стырѧ, и҆ расточи́сте двана́десѧть ѻ҆ве́цъ ᲂу҆чени́ки моѧ̑: можа́хъ вя́щши, не́жели двана́десѧте легеѡ́нѡвъ предста́вити а҆́гг҃лѡвъ, но долготерплю̀, да и҆спо́лнѧтсѧ, ꙗ҆̀же ꙗ҆ви́хъ ва́мъ проро́ки мои́ми, безвѣ́стнаѧ и҆ та́йнаѧ, Гдⷭ҇и сла́ва тебѣ̀.
units.english_cohort_translation: When the lawless took Thee, enduring it, thus didst Thou cry aloud, O Lord: "Though ye have struck the Shepherd, and scattered the twelve sheep, My disciples, yet was I able to summon more than twelve legions of angels; but I am long-suffering, that the things which I revealed unto you through My prophets, the hidden and secret things, might be fulfilled: O Lord, glory be to Thee!"

units.slavonic_incipit: Та́кѡ глаго́летъ Гдⷭ҇ь: прїимꙋ̀ же́злъ мо́й
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: тако глаголет гд прииму жезл мой добрый и
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Та́кѡ глаго́летъ Гдⷭ҇ь: прїимꙋ̀ же́злъ мо́й до́брый, и҆ ѿве́ргꙋ є҆го̀, є҆́же разори́ти завѣ́тъ мо́й, є҆го́же завѣща́хъ, ко всѣ̑мъ лю́демъ: И҆ разори́тсѧ въ де́нь ѻ҆́ный, и҆ ᲂу҆разꙋмѣ́ютъ Ханане́и ѻ҆́вцы храни́мыѧ мнѣ̀, занѐ сло́во Гдⷭ҇не є҆́сть. И҆ рекꙋ̀ къ ни̑мъ: а҆́ще добро̀ пред̾ ва́ми є҆́сть, дади́те мздꙋ̀ мою̀, и҆лѝ ѿрецы́тесѧ: и҆ поста́виша мздꙋ̀ мою̀ три́десѧть сре́бреникъ. И҆ речѐ Гдⷭ҇ь ко мнѣ̀: вложѝ ѧ҆̀ въ горни́ло, и҆ смотрѝ, а҆́ще и҆скꙋше́но є҆́сть, ꙗ҆́коже ѡ҆́бразомъ и҆скꙋше́нъ бы́хъ ѡ҆ ни́хъ. И҆ прїѧ́хъ три́десѧть сре́бреникъ, и҆ вложи́хъ и҆́хъ въ хра́мъ Гдⷭ҇ень въ горни́ло. И҆ ѿверго́хъ же́злъ мо́й вторы́й, ᲂу҆́же, є҆́же разори́ти завѣ́тъ и҆́же посредѣ̀ І҆ꙋ́ды, и҆ посредѣ̀ І҆сра́илѧ. И҆ воззрѧ́тъ на́нь, є҆го́же прокодо́ша. И҆ рекꙋ̀ къ немꙋ̀: что̀ ра̑ны сїѧ̑ посредѣ̀ рꙋкꙋ̑ твоє́ю; И҆ рече́тъ: и҆́миже ᲂу҆ра́ненъ бы́хъ въ домꙋ̀ возлю́бленнагѡ моегѡ̀. Мечꙋ̀, воста́ни на па́стырѧ моегѡ̀, и҆ на мꙋ́жа граждани́на моегѡ̀, глаго́летъ Гдⷭ҇ь Вседержи́тель: поразѝ па́стырѧ, и҆ расточа́тсѧ ѻ҆́вцы ста́да: и҆ наведꙋ̀ рꙋ́кꙋ мою̀ на (ма́лыѧ) па́стыри. И҆ бꙋ́детъ въ де́нь ѻ҆́нъ: не бꙋ́детъ свѣ́тъ, но зима̀ и҆ мра́зъ. И҆ бꙋ́детъ де́нь є҆ди́нъ, и҆ де́нь ѻ҆́нъ зна́емь бꙋ́детъ Гдⷭ҇еви: и҆ не де́нь, и҆ не но́щь, и҆ при ве́черѣ бꙋ́детъ свѣ́тъ. И҆ въ де́нь то́й и҆зы́детъ вода̀ жива̀ и҆з̾ І҆ерꙋсали́ма, по́лꙋ є҆ѧ̀ въ мо́ре пе́рвое, и҆ по́лꙋ є҆ѧ̀ въ мо́ре послѣ́днее; и҆ въ жа́твꙋ, и҆ въ ве́снꙋ бꙋ́детъ та́кѡ. И҆ бꙋ́детъ Гдⷭ҇ь въ Цр҃ѧ по все́й землѝ. Въ де́нь ѻ҆́нъ бꙋ́детъ Гдⷭ҇ь є҆ди́нъ, и҆ и҆́мѧ Гдⷭ҇не є҆ди́но, ѡ҆бходѧ̀ всю̀ зе́млю и҆ пꙋсты́ню. Въ де́нь ѻ҆́нъ бꙋ́детъ є҆́же въ ᲂу҆зда́хъ конѧ̀, ст҃о́е Гдⷭ҇ви Вседержи́телю. И҆ не бꙋ́детъ Ханане́й ктомꙋ̀ въ хра́мѣ Гдⷭ҇а Вседержи́телѧ въ де́нь ѻ҆́нъ.
units.english_cohort_translation: Thus says the Lord: "I will take My goodly staff, and I will cast it away, to break My covenant which I made with all the peoples. And it shall be broken in that day, and the Canaanites, the sheep that are kept for Me, shall know that it is the word of the Lord. And I will say unto them: 'If it be good in your eyes, give Me My price, or refuse it.' And they appointed My price at thirty pieces of silver. And the Lord said unto Me: 'Cast them into the furnace, and see if it be proved, as I was proved by them.' And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them into the house of the Lord, into the furnace. And I cast away My second staff, Binding, that I might break the covenant between Judah and between Israel. And they shall look upon Him Whom they have pierced. And they shall say unto Him: 'What are these wounds in the midst of Thy hands?' And He shall say: 'Those wherewith I was wounded in the house of My beloved.' Awake, O sword, against My shepherd, and against the man that is My fellow, says the Lord Almighty: strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock shall be scattered; and I will bring My hand upon the little shepherds. And it shall come to pass in that day: there shall not be light, but cold and frost. And there shall be one day, and that day shall be known unto the Lord: neither day nor night, and at evening there shall be light. And in that day living water shall go forth out of Jerusalem, half of it toward the former sea, and half of it toward the hinder sea; and in summer and in spring it shall be so. And the Lord shall be King over all the earth. In that day shall the Lord be one, and His name one, encompassing all the earth and the wilderness. In that day that which is upon the bridles of the horses shall be holy unto the Lord Almighty. And there shall no more be a Canaanite in the house of the Lord Almighty in that day."

units.slavonic_incipit: Бра́тїе, мнѣ̀ да не бꙋ́детъ хвали́тисѧ,
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: братие мне да не будет хвалитися токмо о
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Бра́тїе, мнѣ̀ да не бꙋ́детъ хвали́тисѧ, то́кмо ѡ҆ крⷭ҇тѣ̀ Гдⷭ҇а на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хрⷭ҇та̀, и҆́мже мнѣ̀ мі́ръ распѧ́сѧ, и҆ а҆́зъ мі́рꙋ. Ѡ҆ Хрⷭ҇тѣ́ бо І҆и҃сѣ ни ѡ҆брѣ́занїе что̀ мо́жетъ, ни неѡбрѣ́занїе, но нова̀ тва́рь. И҆ є҆ли́цы пра́виломъ си́мъ жи́тельствꙋютъ, ми́ръ на ни́хъ и҆ ми́лость, и҆ на І҆и҃ли Бж҃їи. Про́чее трꙋды̀, да никто́же мѝ дае́тъ: а҆́зъ бо ꙗ҆́звы Гдⷭ҇а І҆и҃са на тѣ́лѣ мое́мъ ношꙋ̀. Бл҃года́ть Гдⷭ҇а на́шегѡ І҆и҃са Хрⷭ҇та̀, со дꙋ́хомъ ва́шимъ бра́тїе, а҆ми́нь.
units.english_cohort_translation: Brethren: God forbid that I should boast, save in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ, by Whom the world is crucified unto me, and I unto the world. For in Christ Jesus neither circumcision avails anything, nor uncircumcision, but a new creation. And as many as walk according to this rule, peace be on them, and mercy, and upon the Israel of God. Henceforth let no man trouble me, for I bear in my body the marks of the Lord Jesus. The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit, brethren. Amen.

units.slavonic_incipit: Во вре́мѧ ѻ҆́но: ᲂу҆́трꙋ бы́вшꙋ, совѣ́тъ
units.slavonic_stem_tier2: во время но утру бывшу совет сотвориша вси
units.slavonic_diplomatic: Во вре́мѧ ѻ҆́но: ᲂу҆́трꙋ бы́вшꙋ, совѣ́тъ сотвори́ша всѝ а҆рхїере́е и҆ ста́рцы людсті́и на І҆и҃са, ꙗ҆́кѡ ᲂу҆би́ти є҆го̀. И҆ свѧза́вше є҆го̀ ведо́ша, и҆ преда́ша є҆го̀ Понті́йскомꙋ Пїла́тꙋ и҆ге́монꙋ. Тогда̀ ви́дѣвъ І҆ꙋ́да преда́вый є҆го̀, ꙗ҆́кѡ ѡ҆сꙋди́ша є҆го̀, раска́ѧвсѧ возвратѝ три́десѧть сре́бреники а҆рхїере́ємъ и҆ ста́рцемъ, глаго́лѧ: согрѣши́хъ, преда́въ кро́вь непови́ннꙋю. Ѻ҆ни́ же рѣ́ша: что̀ є҆́сть на́мъ; ты̀ ᲂу҆́зриши. И҆ пове́ргъ сре́бреники въ це́ркви, ѿи́де, и҆ ше́дъ ᲂу҆дави́сѧ. А҆рхїере́е же прїе́мше сре́бреники рѣ́ша: недосто́йно є҆́сть вложи́ти и҆́хъ въ корва́нꙋ: поне́же цѣна̀ кро́ве є҆́сть. Совѣ́тъ же сотво́рше, кꙋпи́ша и҆́ми село̀ скꙋде́льниче, въ погреба́нїе стра́ннымъ. Тѣ́мже нарече́сѧ село̀ то̀, село̀ кро́ве, да́же до сегѡ̀ днѐ. Тогда̀ сбы́стсѧ рече́нное І҆еремі́емъ проро́комъ, глаго́лющимъ: И҆ прїѧ́ша три́десѧть сре́бреникъ, цѣнꙋ̀ цѣне́ннагѡ, є҆го́же цѣни́ша ѿ сынѡ́въ І҆сра́илевъ, и҆ да́ша ѧ҆̀ на село̀ скꙋде́льниче, ꙗ҆́коже сказа̀ мнѣ̀ Гдⷭ҇ь. І҆и҃съ же ста̀ пред̾ и҆ге́мономъ, и҆ вопросѝ є҆го̀ и҆ге́мѡнъ, глаго́лѧ: ты́ ли є҆сѝ Цр҃ь І҆ꙋде́йскїй; І҆и҃съ же речѐ є҆мꙋ̀: ты̀ глаго́леши. И҆ є҆гда̀ на́нь глаго́лахꙋ а҆рхїере́е и҆ ста́рцы, ничесо́же ѿвѣщава́ше. Тогда̀ глаго́ла є҆мꙋ̀ Пїла́тъ: не слы́шиши ли, коли́кѡ на тѧ̀ свидѣ́тельствꙋютъ; И҆ не ѿвѣща̀ є҆мꙋ̀ ни къ є҆ди́номꙋ глаго́лꙋ, ꙗ҆́кѡ диви́тисѧ и҆ге́монꙋ ѕѣлѡ̀. На всѧ́къ же пра́здникъ ѡ҆бы́чай бѣ̀ и҆ге́мѡнꙋ ѿпꙋща́ти є҆ди́наго наро́дꙋ свѧ́знѧ, є҆го́же хотѧ́хꙋ. И҆мѧ́хꙋ же тогда̀ свѧ́знѧ наро́чита, глаго́лемаго Вара́ввꙋ. Собра́вшымсѧ же и҆̀мъ, речѐ и҆̀мъ Пїла́тъ: кого̀ хо́щете (ѿ ѻ҆бою̀) ѿпꙋщꙋ̀ ва́мъ; Вара́ввꙋ ли, и҆лѝ І҆и҃са глаго́лемаго Хрⷭ҇та̀; Вѣ́дѧше бо, ꙗ҆́кѡ за́висти ра́ди преда́ша є҆го̀. Сѣдѧ́щꙋ же є҆мꙋ̀ на сꙋди́щи, посла̀ къ немꙋ̀ жена̀ є҆гѡ̀, глаго́лющи: ничто́же тебѣ̀ и҆ Пра́ведникꙋ томꙋ̀: мно́гѡ бо пострада́хъ дне́сь въ снѣ̀ є҆гѡ̀ ра́ди. А҆рхїере́е же и҆ ста́рцы навѣсти́ша наро́ды, да и҆спро́сѧтъ Вара́ввꙋ, І҆и҃са же погꙋбѧ́тъ. Ѿвѣща́въ же и҆ге́мѡнъ речѐ и҆̀мъ: кого̀ хо́щете ѿ ѻ҆бою̀ ѿпꙋщꙋ̀ ва́мъ; Ѻ҆ни́ же рѣ́ша: Вара́ввꙋ. Глаго́ла и҆̀мъ Пїла́тъ: что́ ᲂу҆̀бѡ сотворю̀ І҆и҃сꙋ, глаго́лемомꙋ Хрⷭ҇тꙋ̀; Глаго́лаша є҆мꙋ̀ всѝ: да ра́спѧтъ бꙋ́детъ. И҆ге́мѡнъ же речѐ: ко́е ᲂу҆̀бѡ ѕло̀ сотворѝ; Ѻ҆ни́ же и҆́злиха вопїѧ́хꙋ, глаго́люще: да про́пѧтъ бꙋ́детъ. Ви́дѣвъ же Пїла́тъ, ꙗ҆́кѡ ничто́же ᲂу҆спѣва́етъ, но па́че молва̀ быва́етъ, прїе́мъ во́дꙋ, ᲂу҆мы̀ рꙋ́цѣ пред̾ наро́домъ, глаго́лѧ: не пови́ненъ є҆́смь ѿ кро́ве Пра́веднагѡ сегѡ̀: вы̀ ᲂу҆́зрите. И҆ ѿвѣща́вше всѝ лю́дїе рѣ́ша: Кро́вь є҆гѡ̀ на на́съ и҆ на ча́дѣхъ на́шихъ. Тогда̀ ѿпꙋстѝ и҆̀мъ Вара́ввꙋ, І҆и҃са же би́въ, предадѐ и҆̀мъ, да є҆го̀ про́пнꙋтъ. Тогда̀ во́ини и҆ге́мѡновы прїе́мше І҆и҃са на сꙋди́ще, собра́ша на́нь всѐ мно́жество во́ин̆. И҆ совле́кше є҆го̀, ѡ҆дѣ́ѧша є҆го̀ хламѵ́дою червле́ною: и҆ спле́тше вѣне́цъ ѿ те́рнїѧ, возложи́ша на главꙋ̀ є҆гѡ̀, и҆ тро́сть въ десни́цꙋ є҆гѡ̀: и҆ покло́ншесѧ на колѣ́нꙋ пред̾ ни́мъ, рꙋга́хꙋсѧ є҆мꙋ̀, глаго́люще: ра́дꙋйсѧ Цр҃ю̀ І҆ꙋде́йскїй. И҆ плю́нꙋвше на́нь, прїѧ́ша тро́сть, и҆ бїѧ́хꙋ по главѣ̀ є҆гѡ̀. И҆ є҆гда̀ порꙋга́шасѧ є҆мꙋ̀, совлеко́ша съ негѡ̀ багрѧни́цꙋ, и҆ ѡ҆блеко́ша є҆го̀ въ ри̑зы є҆гѡ̀: и҆ ведо́ша є҆го̀ на пропѧ́тїе. И҆сходѧ́ще же ѡ҆брѣто́ша человѣ́ка Кѵрине́йска, и҆́менемъ Сї́мѡна: и҆ семꙋ̀ задѣ́ша понестѝ крⷭ҇тъ є҆гѡ̀. И҆ прише́дше на мѣ́сто нарица́емое Голго́ѳа, є҆́же є҆́сть глаго́лемо кра́нїево мѣ́сто, да́ша є҆мꙋ̀ пи́ти ѻ҆́цетъ съ же́лчїю смѣ́шенъ: и҆ вкꙋси́въ не хотѧ́ше пи́ти. Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremiah the prophet, saying: "And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of Him that was valued, Whom they of the children of Israel did value; and gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord appointed me." And Jesus stood before the governor; and the governor asked Him, saying: "Art Thou the King of the Jews?" And Jesus said unto him: "Thou sayest." And when He was accused by the chief priests and elders, He answered nothing. Then said Pilate unto Him: "Hearest Thou not how many things they witness against Thee?" And He answered him to never a word, insomuch that the governor marveled greatly. Now at that feast the governor was wont to release unto the people a prisoner, whom they would. And they had then a notable prisoner, called Barabbas. Therefore when they were gathered together, Pilate said unto them: "Whom will ye that I release unto you? Barabbas, or Jesus Who is called Christ?" For he knew that for envy they had delivered Him. When he was set down on the judgment seat, his wife sent unto him, saying: "Have thou nothing to do with that just Man; for I have suffered many things this day in a dream because of Him." But the chief priests and elders persuaded the multitude that they should ask Barabbas, and destroy Jesus. The governor answered and said unto them: "Whether of the twain will ye that I release unto you?" They said: "Barabbas." Pilate says unto them: "What shall I do then with Jesus Who is called Christ?" They all say unto him: "Let Him be crucified!" And the governor said: "Why, what evil hath He done?" But they cried out the more, saying: "Let Him be crucified!" When Pilate saw that he could prevail nothing, but that rather a tumult was made, he took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying: "I am innocent of the blood of this just Person: see ye to it."
